It has already been mentioned by me that the three Vedic metres, Gāyatrī, Tṛṣṭup and Jagatī are the sources of origin of the Ambakas (i.e. Kapālas) along with the Vanaspati (i.e. the medicinal herbs). These three metres join together and assume unity (i.e. when they are used in Mantras at the time of the consecration of the Puroḍāśa offerings). That Puroḍāśa is infused with the virility of each of these mantras. Hence the Puroḍāśa is remembered as Trikapāla (having three vessels to hold it). Therefore the Puroḍāśa is Tryambaka as well. Hence the lord (to whom this Puroḍāśa is offered) is remembered as Tryambaka.

## \|\| 1.9.7 \|\|

*dhatte dharmaḥ prajāḥ sarvā mano jñānakaraṃ smṛtam \|*  
*ākṛtiḥ suruce rūpaṃ ruciḥ śraddhākaraḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Dharma sustains all the subjects. Manas is remembered as that which caused knowledge. Ākṛti is the form of splendid beauty. Ruci is remembered as one who inculcates Śraddhā (faith).

## \|\| 1.9.8-9 \|\|

*evamete prajāpālāḥ prajānāṃ sthitihetavaḥ \|*  
*athāsya sṛjataḥ sargaṃ prajānāṃ parivṛddhaye \|\| 8 \|\|*

*na vyavarddhata tāḥ sṛṣṭāḥ prajāḥ kenāpi hetunā \|*  
*tataḥ sa vidadhe buddhimarthaniścayagā minīm \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. Thus these protectors of the subjects are the causes of the sustenance of the subjects.

Even as he continued the creative activity for the sake of the multiplication of the subjects, those created subjects did not increase at all by any means. Therefore, he racked his intellect that should arrive at a decisive conclusion.

## \|\| 1.9.10 \|\|

*athātmani samadrākṣīttamomātrāṃ tu cāriṇīm \|*  
*rajaḥ sattvaṃ parityajya vartamānāṃ svakarmataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Then he saw the Tamas element moving within himself. Thanks to its own action, it had abandoned Rajas and Sattva and was existing by itself.

## \|\| 1.9.11 \|\|

*tataḥ sa tena dukhenaśucaṃ cakre jagatpatiḥ \|*  
*tamaśca vyanudatpaścād rajasātu samāvṛṇot \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Thereupon, due to that sorrow, the lord of the universe felt grieved. He pushed out the Tamas element and afterwards covered it with Rajas.

## \|\| 1.9.12 \|\|

*tattamaḥ pratinuttaṃ vai mithunaṃ saṃprasūyata \|*  
*adharmācaraṇā ttasya hiṃsā śoko vyajāyata \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. That Tamas pushed out by him gave birth to a pair. On account of his unrighteous conduct, Hiṃsā (Violence) and Śoka (grief) were born.

## \|\| 1.9.13 \|\|

*tatastasminsamudbhūte mithune varaṇātmake \|*  
*tataḥ sa bhagavānāsīt prītaścaitaṃ hi śiśriye \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When that pair in the form of Varaṇa (covering up), was born, the lord became delighted. He resorted to this.

## \|\| 1.9.14 \|\|

*evaṃ prītātmanastasya svadehārddhādviniḥsṛtā \|*  
*nārī paramakalyāṇī sarvabhūtamanoharā \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. From a half of the body of the lord who was delighted within himself thus, a woman conducive to great welfare, and charming and fascinating to all living beings, came out.

## \|\| 1.9.15 \|\|

*sā hi kāmātmanā sṛṣṭā prakṛteḥ sā surūpiṇī \|*  
*śatarūpeti sā proktā sā proktaiva punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. That beautiful looking lady was indeed created from Prakṛti by him (as he was) desirous (of progeny) and was called Śatarūpā. And she was again and again called so.

## \|\| 1.9.16 \|\|

*tataḥ prajāḥ samudbhūtā yathā proktā mayā purā \|*  
*prakriyāyāṃ yathā tubhyaṃ tretāmadhye mahātmanaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. It was then that the subjects were born of that noble-souled being in the middle of Tretā yuga as has already been mentioned by me to you in section-I Prakriyāpāda.

## \|\| 1.9.17 \|\|

*yadā prajāstu tāḥ sṛṣṭā na vyavaddhata dhīmataḥ \|*  
*tato 'nyānmānasānputrānātmanaḥ sadṛśo 'sṛjata \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. When those subjects created by that intelligent self-possessed being did not increase in number, he created other mental sons similar to himself.

## \|\| 1.9.18-19 \|\|

*bhṛgvaṅgiromarīcīṃśca pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum \|*  
*dakṣamatriṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca nirmame mānasānsutān \|\| 18 \|\|*

*nava brahmāṇa ityete purāṇe niścayaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*brahmā yatātmakānāṃ tu sarveṣāmātmayoninām \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. He created these nine mental sons viz.: Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Marīci, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Dakṣa, Atri and Vasiṣṭha. In the Purāṇa, these are decisively called the “nine Brahmās” (because they were like) Brahmā (the creator) unto all beings of controlled souls, having the Ātman as their source of origin.

## \|\| 1.9.20 \|\|

*tato 'sṛjatpunarbrahmā dharmaṃ bhūtasukhāvaham \|*  
*prajāpatiṃ ruciṃ caiva pūrveṣāmeva pūrvajau \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Then Brahmā created again Dharma who was delightful and pleasant unto all living beings; as well as the Prajāpati Ruci. These two were the eldest of all ancient ones.

## \|\| 1.9.21 \|\|

*buddhitaḥ sasṛje dharmaṃ sarvabhūtasukhāvaham \|*  
*manasastu rucirnāma jajñe jo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. He created from his intellect, Dharma who was delightful and pleasant unto all living beings. He who is named Ruci was born of the mind of (the lord of) unmanifest birth.

## \|\| 1.9.22-24 \|\|

*bhṛgustu tdṛdayājjajñe ṛṣiḥ sālalayoninaḥ \|*  
*prāṇāddakṣaṃ sṛjanbrahmā cakṣurbhyāṃ tu marīcinam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*abhimānātmakaṃ rudraṃ nirmame nīlalohitam \|*  
*śirasoṃgirasaṃ caiva śrotrādatriṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

*pulastyaṃ ca tathodānādvyānācca pulahaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*samānajo vasiṣṭhaśca hyapānānnirmame kratum \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. Sage Bhṛgu was born of the heart of the lord whose source of origin was water. Brahmā created Dakṣa from his vital breath and Marīci from his eyes. He created Rudra (also known as) Nīlalohita in the form of Abhimāna (prestige, honour). He created aṅgiras from his head and Atri from the ears. From his Udāna (?) vital breath (prāṇa) he created Pulastya and Pulaha from Vyāna. Vasiṣṭha was born of Samāna and he created Kratu from Apāna.

## \|\| 1.9.25 \|\|

*ityete brahmaṇaḥ putrāḥ prajādau dvādaśa smṛtāḥ \|*  
*dharmasteṣāṃ prathamajo devatānāṃ smṛtastu vai \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Thus these twelve are remembered as the sons of Brahmā at the beginning (of creation) of subjects. Dharma was the first-born among those Devatās.

## \|\| 1.9.26 \|\|

*bhṛgvādayastu ye sṛṣṭāste vai brahmarṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*gṛhamedhipurāṇāste dharmastaiḥ prāk pravarttitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Bhrgu and others who had been created are remembered as Brahmarṣis (Brahminical sages). They are the ancient house-holders and Dharma (virtue) was initially established by them.

## \|\| 1.9.27-29 \|\|

*dvādaśaite prasūyante prajāḥ kalpe punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ dvādaśa te vaṃśā divyā devaguṇānvitāḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kriyāvantaḥ prajāvanto maharṣibhiralaṅkṛtāḥ \|*  
*yadā tairiha sṛṣṭaistu dharmmādyaiśca maharṣibhiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sṛjyamānāḥ prajāścaiva na vyavarddhanta dhīmataḥ \|*  
*tamomātrāvṛtaḥ so 'bhūcchokapratihataśca vai \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-28a. In the Kalpa, these twelve give birth to subjects again and again. Their twelve races arc divine and equipped with Divine qualities. They perform holy rites and have (i.e. procreate) progeny. They are adorned (honoured) by great sages.

28b-29. When the progeny created by Dharma and other great sages (who themselves) had been created (by him) did not multiply, the intelligent and self-possessed lord became slightly enveloped by Tamas and afflicted by grief.

## \|\| 1.9.30 \|\|

*yathā'vṛtaḥ sa vai brahmā tamomātrā tu sā punaḥ \|*  
*putrāṇāṃ ca tamomātrā aparā niḥsṛtābhavat \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Just as Brahmā was enveloped by Tamas elements, so also in the case of his sons too another Tamas element issued forth.

## \|\| 1.9.31-32 \|\|

*pratisrotātmako 'dharmo hiṃsā caivāśubhātmikā \|*  
*tataḥ pratihate tasya pratīte varaṇātmake \|\| 31 \|\|*

*svāṃ tanuṃ sa tadā brahmā samapohata bhāsvarām \|*  
*dvidhā kṛtvā svakaṃ dehamarddhena puruṣo 'bhavat \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Adharma is in the nature of return flow (?) and Hiṃsā (Violence) is inauspicious by nature. Then when he was obstructed and the nature of the covering was manifest, Brahmā discarded his own shining physical body. After dividing his own body into two, he became a man by one half.

## \|\| 1.9.33 \|\|

*ardhena nārī sā tasya śatarūpā vyajāyata \|*  
*prakṛtirbhūtadhātrī sā kāmādvai sṛjataḥ prabhoḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. By (another) half he became a woman and she was Śatarūpā. She was the Prakṛti, the mother of all living beings (and manifested thus) because the lord was creating out of desire.

## \|\| 1.9.34-36 \|\|

*sā divaṃ pṛthivīṃ caiva mahimnā vyāpya susthitā \|*  
*brahmāṇaḥ sā tanuḥ pūrvā divamāvṛtya tiṣṭataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*yā tvarddhā sṛjyate nārī śatarūpā vyajāyata \|*  
*sā devī niyutaṃ taptvā tapaḥ parama duścaram \|\| 35 \|\|*

*bharttāraṃ dīptayaśasaṃ puruṣaṃ pratyapadyata \|*  
*sa vai svāyaṃbhuvaḥ pūrvaṃ puruṣo manurucyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. With her grandeur, she pervaded the firmament and the earth and remained steady. That was the former body of Brahmā who stayed enveloping the firmament. The half that was created as a woman became Śatarūpā. That divine lady performed a very difficult penance for a hundred thousand years and obtained Puruṣa of brilliant fame as her husband. Indeed, he is called Manu, the Puruṣa, the earlier son of the self-born lord.

## \|\| 1.9.37-40 \|\|

*tasyaikasaptatiyugaṃ manvantaramihocyate \|*  
*labdhvā tu puruṣaḥ patnīṃ śatarūpāmayonijām \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tayā sa ramate sārddhaṃ tasmātsā ratirucyate \|*  
*prathamaḥ saṃprayogaḥ sa kalpādau samavarttata \|\| 38 \|\|*

*virājamasṛjadbrahmā so 'bhavatpuruṣo virāṭ \|*  
*samrāṭ saśatarūpastu vairājastu manuḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sa vairājaḥ prajāsargaṃ sasarja puruṣo manuḥ \|*  
*vairājātpuruṣādvīrau śatarūpā vyajāyata \|\| 40 \|\|*

37-38a. Seventy-one sets of four Yugas constitute what is called his Manvantara (reign of a Manu). After obtaining as h is wife, Śatarūpā who was not born of any womb, the Puruṣa sported with her. Hence it is called Rati (sexual dalliance).

38b-40. The first union took place in the beginning of the Kalpa. Brahmā created Virāṭ (the immense Being). That Virāṭ became the Puruṣa. He, accompanied by Śatarūpā, is remembered as Vairāja, Manu and Samrāṭ (Emperor). That Puruṣa, Manu, the Vairāja created subjects (begot progeny). From Vairāja, the Puruṣa, Śatarūpā gave birth to two heroic sons.

## \|\| 1.9.41 \|\|

*priyavratottānapādau putrau putravatāṃ varau \|*  
*kanye dve sumahābhāge yābhyāṃ jātā imāḥ prajāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. They were Priyavrata and Uttānapāda. These two sons were the most excellent sons that persons possessing sons could expect. (She gave birth to) two daughters also of great fortune. From them these subjects were born.

## \|\| 1.9.42 \|\|

*devī nāmnā tathākūliḥ prasūtiścaiva te śubhe \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuvaḥ prasūtiṃ tu dakṣāya vyasṛjatprabhuḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. They were the divine lady named Ākūti and auspicious lady Prasūti. Boíh of them were auspicious. The lordly sou of the self-born lord gave Prasūti to Dakṣa.

## \|\| 1.9.43 \|\|

*ruceḥ prajāpateścaiva ākūtiṃ pratya pādayat \|*  
*ākūtyāṃ mithunaṃ jajñe mānasasya ruceḥ śubham \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. He gave Ākūti to Ruci, the Prajāpati. An auspicious pair was born of Ākūti as the progeny of Ruci, the mental son (of Brahmā).

## \|\| 1.9.44 \|\|

*yajñaśca dakṣiṇā caiva yamalau tau babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*yajñasya dakṣiṇāyāṃ ca putrā dvādaśa jajñire \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. They were the twins Yajña and Dakṣiṇā. Twelve sons were born to Yajña and Dakṣiṇā.

## \|\| 1.9.45 \|\|

*yāmā iti samākhyātā devāḥ svāyaṃbhuvetare \|*  
*yamasya putrā yajñasya tasmādyāmāstu te smṛtāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. They were the Devas named Yāmas in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara. They were the sons of twins, viz: Yajña and Dakṣiṇā. Hence they are remembered as Yāmas.

## \|\| 1.9.46 \|\|

*ajitāścaiva śukrāśca dvau gaṇau brahmaṇaḥ smṛtau \|*  
*yāmāḥ pūrvaṃ parikrāntā yeṣāṃ saṃjñā divaukasaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. (?) Two groups of Brahmā are remembered viz: Ajitas and Śukras. The Yāmas who have the appellation Dīvaukas (heaven-dwellers) circumambulated the former.

## \|\| 1.9.47 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhūva sutāyāṃ tu prasūtyāṃ lokamātaraḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃ kanyāścaturviṃśaddakṣastvajanayatprabhuḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. Lord Dakṣa begot of Prasūti, the daughter of Svāyambhuva Manu, twenty-four daughters who became mothers of the world.

## \|\| 1.9.48-50 \|\|

*sarvāstāśca mahābhāgāḥ sarvāḥ kamalalocanāḥ \|*  
*yogapatnyaśca tāḥ sarvāḥ sarvāstā yogamātaraḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*sarvāśca brahmavādinyaḥ sarvā viśvasya mātaraḥ \|*  
*śraddhā lakṣmīrdhṛtistuṣṭiḥ puṣṭirmedhā tathā kriyā \|\| 49 \|\|*

*buddhirlajjā vasuḥ śāntiḥ siddhiḥ kīrttistrayodaśa \|*  
*patnyarthaṃ pratijagrāha dharmo dākṣāyaṇīḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

48-49a. All of them were highly fortunate. All of them were lotus-eyed. All of them were wives of Yogins and all of them were Yogic mothers. All of them were expounders of Brahman and all of them were the mothers of the universe.

49b-50. Lord Dharma accepted (the following) thirteen daughters of Dakṣa as his wives, viz: Śraddhā, Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Medhā, Kriyā, Buddhi, Lajjā, Vasu, Śānti, Siddhi, and Kīrti as the thirteenth.

## \|\| 1.9.51-52 \|\|

*dvārāṇyetāni caivāsya vihitāni svayaṃbhuvā \|*  
*yānyāḥ śiṣṭā yavīyasya ekādaśa sulocanāḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*satī khyātiśca saṃbhūtiḥ smṛtiḥ prītiḥ kṣamā tathā \|*  
*sannatiścānasūyā ca ūrjā svāhā svadhā tathā \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. These door-ways of his (creative activity) were ordained by the self-born lord. The others that remained were the eleven younger daughters of beautiful eyes, viz: Satī,. Khyāti, Sambhūti, Smṛti, Prīti, Kṣamā, Sannati, Anasūyā, Ūrjā, Svāhā and Svadhā.

## \|\| 1.9.53-54 \|\|

*tāstadā pratyagṛhṇanta punaranye mahārṣayaḥ \|*  
*rudro bhṛgurmarīciśca aṅgirāḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*pulastyo 'trirvasiṣṭhaśca pitaro 'gristathaiva ca \|*  
*satīṃ bhavāya prāyacchatkhyātiṃ ca bhṛgave tathā \|\| 54 \|\|*

53-54. Other great sages accepted them (as wives). They were Rudra, Bhṛgu, Marīci, Aṅgiras, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Agni and Pitṛs. He gave (in marriage) Satī to Bhava and Khyāti to Bhṛgu.

## \|\| 1.9.55 \|\|

*marīcaye tu saṃbhūtiṃ smṛtimaṅgirase dadau \|*  
*prītiṃ caiva pulastyāya kṣamāṃ vai pulahāya ca \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. To Marīci, he gave Sambhūti, and Smṛti to Aṅgiras To Pulastya he gave Prīti and Kṣamā to Pulaha.

## \|\| 1.9.56 \|\|

*kratave saṃtatiṃ nāma anasūyāṃ tathātraye \|*  
*ūrjāṃ dadau vasiṣṭhāya svāhāṃ caivāgnaye dadau \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. To Kratu, he gave Sannati and the (daughter) named Anasūyā to Atri. He gave Ūrjā to Vasiṣṭha and Svāhā to Agni (the fire-god).

## \|\| 1.9.57-58 \|\|

*svadhāṃ caiva pitṛbhyastu tāsvapatyāni me śṛṇu \|*  
*etāḥ sarvā mahābhāgāḥ prajāstvanusṛtāḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*manvantareṣu sarveṣu yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|*  
*śraddhā kāmaṃ prajajñe 'tha darpo lakṣmī sutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. He gave Svadhā to the Pitṛs. Listen from me their children. All these were highly fortunate ladies; their subjects (children) obediently followed them in all Manvantaras till the time of ultimate annihilation (of the world). Śraddhā gave birth to Kāma and Darpa (arrogance) is remembered as the son of Lakṣmī.

## \|\| 1.9.59 \|\|

*dhṛtyāstu niyamaḥ putrastuṣṭyāḥ saṃtoṣa ucyate \|*  
*puṣṭyā lābhaḥ sutaścāpi medhāputraḥ śrutastathā \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Niyama (Restraint) was the son of Dhṛti (Courage). Santoṣa (Contentment) is mentioned as the son of Tuṣṭi (Satisfaction). Lābha (gain) was the son of Puṣṭi (Nourishment) and Śruta (Learning) was the son of Medhā (Intellect).

## \|\| 1.9.60 \|\|

*kriyāyāstanayau proktau damaśca śama eva ca \|*  
*buddherbodhaḥ sutaścāpi apramādaśca tāvubhau \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Dama (Restraint of sense-organs) and Śama (Restraint of the mind) are mentioned as the sons of Kriyā (Activity). Bodha (Understanding) and Apramāda (Absence of Errors) were the sons of Buddhi (Intellect).

## \|\| 1.9.61 \|\|

*lajjāyā vinayaḥ putro vyavasāyo vasoḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*kṣemaḥ śānteḥ sutaścāpi sukhaṃ siddhervyajāyata \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Vinaya (Modesty) was the son of Lajjā (Bashfulness). Vyavasāya (Enterprise) was the son of Vasu. Kṣema (Welfare) was the son of Śānti (Tranquility). Sukha (Happiness) was born of Siddhi (Achievement).

## \|\| 1.9.62 \|\|

*yaśaḥ kīrteḥ sutaścāpi ityete dharmasūnavaḥ \|*  
*kāmasya tu suto harṣo devyāṃ siddhyāṃ vyajāyata \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. Yaśas (Fame) was the son of Kīrti (Renown)—These were the sons of Dharma. Kāma’s (Love’s) son Harṣa (Delight) was born of the noble lady Siddhi (Achievement).

## \|\| 1.9.63 \|\|

*ityeṣa vai sukhodarkaḥ sargo dharmasya sāttvikaḥ \|*  
*jajñe hiṃsā tvadharmādvai nikṛtiṃ cānṛtaṃ ca te \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Through Adharma (Evil), Hiṃsā (Violence) gave birth to the two children Nikṛti (Dishonesty, Wickedness) and Anṛta (Falsehood).

## \|\| 1.9.64 \|\|

*nikṛtyanṛtayorjajña bhayaṃ naraka eva ca \|*  
*māyā ca vedanā cāpi mithunadvayametayoḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Two twins were born of Nikṛti and Anṛta viz Bhaya (Fear), Naraka (Hell), Māyā (Illusion) and Vedanā (Pain).

## \|\| 1.9.65 \|\|

*mayājjajñe 'tha vai māyā mṛtyuṃ bhūtāpahāriṇam \|*  
*vedanāyāṃ tataścāpi jejña duḥkhaṃ tu rauravāt \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Through Maya, Māyā gave birth to Mṛtyu (Death) that takes away all living beings. Then Duḥkha (Misery) was born of Vedanā through Raurava (Hell).

## \|\| 1.9.66 \|\|

*mṛtyorvyādhirjarāśokakrodhāsūyā vijajñire \|*  
*duḥkhottarāḥ smṛtā hyete sarve cādharmalakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Vyādhi (Sickness) gave birth to Jarā (Old age), Śoka (Grief), Krodha (Anger) and Asūyā (Jealousy) through Mṛtyu. All these are remembered as characteristics of Adharma (Evil) with misery as the ultimate end.

## \|\| 1.9.67 \|\|

*teṣāṃ bhāryāsti putro vā sarve hyanidhanāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*ityeṣa tāmasaḥ sargo jajñe dharmaniyā makaḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. Their wife, son,—everyone is remembered as deathless.

Thus this Tāmasa creation took birth with Adharma as the controlling one.

## \|\| 1.9.68 \|\|

*prajāḥ sṛceti vyādiṣṭo brahmaṇā nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*so 'bhidhyāya satīṃ bhāryāṃ nirmame cātmasaṃbhavān \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Nīlalohita was commanded by Brahmā, “Beget progeny”. He contemplated on his wife Satī and created sons.

## \|\| 1.9.69 \|\|

*nādhikānna ca hīnāstānmānasānātmanā samān \|*  
*sahasraṃ ca sahasrāṇāmasṛjatkṛttivāsasaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. They were neither superior to him nor inferior. They were his mental sons on a par with himself. He created thousands and thousands of such children wearing elephant hides.

## \|\| 1.9.70-80 \|\|

*tulyānevātmanā sarvān rūpatejobala śrutaiḥ \|*  
*piṅgalānsaniṣaṅgāṃśca kapardī nīlalohitān \|\| 70 \|\|*

*viśikhānhīnakeśāṃśca dṛṣṭighnāstānkapālinaḥ \|*  
*mahārūpānvirūpāṃśca viśvarūpāśca rūpiṇaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*rathino varmiṇaścaiva dhanvino 'tha varūthinaḥ \|*  
*sahasraśatabāhūṃśca divyabhaumāntarikṣagān \|\| 72 \|\|*

*sthūla śīrṣānaṣṭadaṃṣṭrān dvijihvāṃstu trilocanān \|*  
*annādānpiśitādāṃśca ājyapānsomapostathā \|\| 73 \|\|*

*atimeḍhrograkāyāṃśca śitikaṇṭhogramanyukān \|*  
*saniṣaṅgatanutrāṃśca dhanvino hyasicarmiṇaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*āsīnān dhāvataścāpi jṛṃbhataścāpyadhiṣṭhitān \|*  
*adhīyānāśca japato yuñjato dhyāyatastathā \|\| 75 \|\|*

*jvalato varṣataścaiva dyotamānānpradhūpitān \|*  
*buddhānbuddhatamāṃścaiva brahmasvān brahmadarśinaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*nīlagrīvānsahasrākṣān sarvāṃścaiva kṣamācarān \|*  
*adṛśyānsarvabhūtānāṃ mahāyogānmahaujasaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*rudato dravataścaiva evaṃ yuktānsahasraśaḥ \|*  
*ayātayāmān sṛjataṃ rudrametānsurottamān \|\| 78 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā brahmābravīdenaṃ māsrākṣīrīdṛśīḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*na sraṣṭavyātmana stalyā prajā naivādhikā tathā \|\| 79 \|\|*

*anyāḥ sṛjasva bhadraṃ te prajāstvaṃ mṛtyusaṃyutāḥ \|*  
*nārabhante hi karmāṇi prajā vigatamṛtyavaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

70-80. All of them had these characteristics and features: All of them were on a par with himself in form, brilliance, strength and learning. They were tawny-coloured. They had quivers and matted hair. They were dark blue-red in complexion. They were devoid of tufts. They had no hairs. They were killers with eyes (by casting a look). They had Kapālas (skills) with them. They had huge beautiful forms and hideous cosmic forms. Some occupied chariots and wore coats of mail. They were defenders wearing armours. They had hundreds and thousands of arms. They were able to go through the firmament, earth and heaven; they had big heads, eight fangs, two tongues and three eyes. (Some were) eaters of rice, (some) eaters of flesh, (some) drinkers of ghee and (some of) Soma juice. (Some) had penises of great size; fierce bodies and blue necks. Some had fierce fury. They had quivers and armours, bows, swords and leather shields. Some were seated; some were running. Some yawning and some occupying (seats). Some were reciting (the Vedas), some performing Japas, Yogic practices and meditations. Some were blazing. Some were showering, some shining and some smoking. Some were enlightened. Some were wakeful, alert and enlightened. Some had the property of Brahmā (?). Some had the vision of Brahman. They had blue necks and thousand eyes. All of them were walking over the earth. They were invisible to all living beings. They had great Yogic power, virility and splendour. They were shouting and running. On seeing Rudra creating these excellent Devas with these qualities and features, in thousands even before the expiry of the period of a Yāma, Brahmā told him—“Do not create subjects like these. The subjects should not be created on a par with oneself or superior to oneself; welfare unto you. Create other subjects vulnerable to death. Subjects devoid of death do not begin to perform holy-rites”.

## \|\| 1.9.81 \|\|

*evasukto 'bravīdenaṃ nāhaṃ mṛtyujarānvitāḥ \|*  
*prajāḥ srakṣyāmi bhadraṃ te sthito 'haṃ tvaṃ sṛja prabho \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Thus addressed, he (Rudra) said to him (Brahmā): “I will not create progeny subject to death and old age. Prosperity unto you. I am standing by (i.e. cease to procreate); you please create, O lord.

## \|\| 1.9.82 \|\|

*ete ye vai mayā sṛṣṭā virūpā nīlalohitāḥ \|*  
*sahasraṃ hi sahasrāṇāmātmano mama niḥsṛtāḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. These hideous and bluish-red coloured subjects who had been created by me in thousands and thousands, have come out of my own self.

## \|\| 1.9.83 \|\|

*ete devā bhaviṣyanti rudrā nāma mahābalāḥ \|*  
*pṛthivyāmantarikṣe ca rudrāṇyastāḥ pariśrutāḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. These Devas will be known by the name of Rudras. They are highly powerful. Those Rudrāṇīs are well-known over the earth and firmament.

## \|\| 1.9.84 \|\|

*śatarudre samāmnātā bhaviṣyantīha yajñiyāḥ \|*  
*yajñabhājo bhaviṣyanti sarve devagaṇaiḥ saha \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Enumerated in the (Veḍic text) Śatarudra, they will become worthy of Yajñas. All of them will partake of the Yajñas along with the groups of Devas.

## \|\| 1.9.85 \|\|

*manvantareṣu ye devā bhaviṣyantīha chandajāḥ \|*  
*taiḥ sārddhamijyamānāste sthāsyantīhāyugakṣayāt \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Till the end of the Yuga, they will remain, on being worshipped along with those Devas born of Cchandas (Vedas or—born as they are pleased) in the Manvantaras.

## \|\| 1.9.86 \|\|

*evamuktastato brahmā mahādevena sa prabhuḥ \|*  
*pratyuvāca tathā bhīmaṃ tdṛṣyamāṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. On being told thus by Mahādeva, that lord Brahmā, the delighted lord of subjects replied to the terrible Rudra.

## \|\| 1.9.87 \|\|

*evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ te yathā te vyātdṛtaṃ prabho \|*  
*brahmaṇā samanu jñāte tataḥ sarvamabhūtkila \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. “O lord welfare unto you. Let it be as spoken by you.”

When it was permitted by Brahmā, everything happened that way.

## \|\| 1.9.88 \|\|

*tataḥ prabhṛti devaḥ sa na prāsūyata vai prajāḥ \|*  
*ūrdhvaretāḥ sthitaḥ sthāṇuryāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. Thenceforth, the lord Sthānu did not beget subjects. He remained celibate till the ultimate annihilation.

## \|\| 1.9.89-92 \|\|

*yasmātproktaṃ sthito 'smīti tasmātsthāṇurbudhaiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*jñānaṃ tapaśca satyaṃ ca hyaiśvaryaṃ dharma eva ca \|\| 89 \|\|*

*vairāgyamātmasaṃbodhaḥ kṛtsnānyetāni śaṅkare \|*  
*sarvāndevānṛṣīṃścaiva sametānasuraiḥ saha \|\| 90 \|\|*

*atyeti tejasā devo mahādevastataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*atyeti devā naiśvaryādvalena ca mahāsurān \|\| 91 \|\|*

*jñānena ca munīnsarvānyogādbhūtāni sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*evameva mahādevaḥ sarvadevanamaskṛtaḥ \|*  
*prajāmanu dyāmāṃ sṛṣṭvā sargādupararāma ha \|\| 92 \|\|*

89-91a. He is remembered by learned man as Sthāṇu because it was said by him thus—“I am standing by”. All these qualities are present in Śaṅkara—viz: knowledge, penance, truthfulness, glorious prosperity, virtue, detachment and comprehension. of the self. He excels all the Devas and sages along with the Asuras, by means of his splendour. Hence the lord is remembered as Mahādeva (Great god).

91b-92. He excels the Devas through his glorious prosperity, the great Asuras through his power, all the sages through his knowledge and all the living beings through Yoga. It is thus that Mahādeva is bowed to by all the Devas. After creating the subjects devoid of enterprise, he refrained from creation.

## Chapter 10 - Magnificence of God Śiva: birth of Nīlalohita

## \|\| 1.10.1 \|\|

*ṛṣiruvāca*  
*asminkalpe tvayā noktaḥ prādurbhāvo mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*mahādevasya rudrasya sādhakairṛṣibhiḥ saha \|\| 1 \|\|*

Summary: Magnificence of God Śiva: Birth of Nīlalohita: His eight Names and Forms.

Note: This chapter deals with the eight forms of god Śiva—a popular conception in Purāṇas and classical literature. It is an amplification of a similar concept in Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa as noted below. This chapter is textually very close to Vā.p. Chapter 27.

The Sage said:

1\. The manifestation in this Kalpa of the noble-souled great lord Rudra along with the Sādhaka (spiritual aspirants) has not been narrated by you.

Sūta replied:

## \|\| 1.10.2 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*utpattirādisargasya mayā proktā samāsataḥ \|*  
*vistareṇa pravakṣyāmi nāmāni tanubhiḥ saha \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The origin of the primordial creation has been succinctly mentioned by me. I shall now narrate in detail the names along with the physical bodies.

## \|\| 1.10.3 \|\|

*patnīṣu janayāmāsa mahādevaḥ sutānbahūna \|*  
*kalpeṣvanyeṣvatīteṣu hyasminkalpe tu tāñśṛṇu \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. Mahādeva begot of his wives many sons in the other Kalpas that have passed by. Listen to those (procreated) in this Kalpa.

## \|\| 1.10.4 \|\|

*kalpādāvātmanastulyaṃ sutamadhyāyata prabhuḥ \|*  
*prādurā sīttatoṅke 'sya kumāro nīlalohitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. In the beginning of the Kalpa, the lord contemplated on a son on a par with himself. Thereafter, the child Nīlalohita appeared on his lap.

## \|\| 1.10.5-6 \|\|

*ruroda susvaraṃ ghoraṃ nirdahanniva tejasā \|*  
*dṛṣṭvā rudantaṃ sahasā kumāraṃ nīlalohitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kiṃ rodiṣi kumāreti brahmā taṃ pratyabhāṣata \|*  
*so 'bravīddehi me nāma prathamaṃ tvaṃ pitāmaha \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. He cried loudly in a terrible manner (voice). He appeared as though he would burn by means of his briliance. On seeing the child Nīlalohita crying suddenly, Brahmā spoke to him—“Why do you cry, O child?” He replied—“Give me at the outset a name, O Grandfather.”

## \|\| 1.10.7 \|\|

*rudrastvaṃ deva nāmāsi sa ityukto 'rudatpunaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ rodiṣi kumāreti brahmā taṃ pratyabhāṣata \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. “O lord, you are named Rudra”. On being told thus he cried again. “Why do you cry, O child?” asked Brahmā to him.

## \|\| 1.10.8 \|\|

*nāma dehi dvitīyaṃ me ityuvāca svayaṃbhuvam \|*  
*bhavastvaṃ devanāmnāsi ityuktaḥ so 'rudatpunaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. “Give me a second name”, said he to the self-born Lord. “You are Bhava byname, O Lord”. On being told thus he cried again.

## \|\| 1.10.9 \|\|

*kiṃ rodiṣīti taṃ brahmā rudantaṃ pratyuvāca ha \|*  
*tṛtīyaṃ dehi me nāma ityuktaḥ so 'bravītpunaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. “Why do you cry?”, enquired Brahmā of the crying child. “Give me a third name”. On being told thus, he said again.

## \|\| 1.10.10 \|\|

*śarvastvaṃ deva nāmnāsi ityuktaḥ so 'rudatpunaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ rodiṣīti taṃ brahmā rudantaṃ pratyuvāca ha \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. “O lord, you are Śarva by name.” On being told thus he cried again, “Why do you cry?”, asked Brahmā again to the crying child.

## \|\| 1.10.11 \|\|

*caturtha dehi me nāma ityuktaḥ so 'bravītpunaḥ \|*  
*īśāno devanāmnāsi ityuktaḥ so 'rudatpunaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. “Give me a fourth name.” On being told thus, he said again, “O lord, you are īśāna by name”. On being told thus he cried again.

## \|\| 1.10.12 \|\|

*kiṃ rodiṣīti taṃ brahmā rudantaṃ punarabravīt \|*  
*pañcamaṃ nāma dehīti pratyuvāca svayaṃbhuvam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. “Why do you cry”, said Brahmā to that crying child again. He replied to the self-born lord—“Give me a fifth name.”

## \|\| 1.10.13 \|\|

*paśūnāṃ tvaṃ patirdeva ityuktaḥ so 'rudatpunaḥ \|*  
*kiṃ rodiṣīti taṃ brahmā rudantaṃ punarabravīt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. “You are the lord and master of all Paśus (Animals, living beings)”. On being told thus, he cried again. “Why do you cry?” said Brahmā to that crying child, once again.

## \|\| 1.10.14 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭhaṃ vai dehi me nāma ityuktaḥ pratyuvāca tam \|*  
*bhīmastvaṃ deva nāmnāsi ityuktaḥ so 'rudatpunaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. “Indeed, give me the sixth name”. On being told thus he replied to him—“O lord, you are Bhīma by name”. On being told thus he cried again.

## \|\| 1.10.15 \|\|

*kiṃ rodiṣīti taṃ brahmā rudantaṃ punarabravīt \|*  
*saptamaṃ dehi me nāma ityuktaḥ pratyuvāca ha \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. “Why do you cry?”, asked Brahmā again to that crying child. “Give me the seventh name”. On being told thus he replied:

## \|\| 1.10.16 \|\|

*ugrastvaṃ deva nāmnāsi ityuktaḥ so 'rudatpunaḥ \|*  
*taṃ rudantaṃ kumāraṃ tu mārodīriti so 'bravīt \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. “O lord, you are Ugra by name”. On being told thus, he cried again. To that crying child he said—“Da not cry”.

## \|\| 1.10.17 \|\|

*so 'bravīdaṣṭamaṃ nāma dehi me tvaṃ vibho punaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ mahādevanāmāsi ityukto virarāma ha \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. He said—“Give me, O lord, the eighth name”. “You are Mahādeva by name”. On being told thus, he stopped crying.

## \|\| 1.10.18 \|\|

*labdhvā nāmāni caitāni brahmāṇaṃ nīlalohitaḥ \|*  
*provāca nāmnāmeteṣāṃ sthānāni pradiśeti ha \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. After securing these names. Nīlalohita requested Brahmā—“Indicate the abodes of these names”.

## \|\| 1.10.19-20 \|\|

*tato visṛṣṭāstanava eṣāṃ nāmnā svayaṃbhuvā \|*  
*sūryo jalaṃ mahī vāyurva hnirākāśameva ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dīkṣitā brāhmaṇaścandra ityevaṃ te 'ṣṭadhā tanuḥ \|*  
*teṣu pūjyaśca vandyaśca namaskāryaśca yatnataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Then the bodies were allotted by the self-bora lord unto these names (abodes). They were—the sun, the water, the earth, the wind, the fire, the Ether, the initiated Brāhmaṇa and the Moon. Thus the bodies were of eight varieties. The lord is to be worshipped, saluted and bowed to in those bodies.

## \|\| 1.10.21-23 \|\|

*provāca taṃ punarbrahmā kumāraṃ nīlalohitam \|*  
*yaduktaṃ te mayā pūrvaṃ nāma rudreti vai vibho \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tasyādityatanurnāmnaḥ prathamā prathamasya te \|*  
*ityukte tasya yattejaścakṣustvāsītprakāśakam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*viveśa tattadādityaṃ tasmādrudro hyasau smṛtaḥ \|*  
*udyatamastaṃ yantaṃ ca varjayeddarśaneravim \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Brahmā said again to the child Nīlalohita—“O lord, at the outset, your name has been mentioned by me as Rudra. The sun shall be the first body unto thy first name”. When this was uttered his splendour became an eye, which illuminates, then it entered the sun. Hence he (the sun) is remembered as Rudra. One shall avoid seeing the sun while rising or while setting.

## \|\| 1.10.24 \|\|

*śaśvacca jāyate yasmācchaśvatsaṃtiṣṭhate tu yat \|*  
*tasmātmūryaṃ na vīkṣeta āyuṣkāmaḥ śuciḥ sadā \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Since the sun comes into view frequently and since it vanishes frequently, one, who desires for longevity, should not directly see the sun. One should always be pure.

## \|\| 1.10.25-26 \|\|

*atītānāgataṃ rudraṃ viprā hyāpyāyayanti yat \|*  
*ubhe saṃdhye hyupāsīnā gṛṇantaḥ sāmaṛgyajuḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*udyansa tiṣṭhate ṛkṣu madhyāhne ca yajuḥṣvatha \|*  
*sāmasvathāparāhṇe tu rudraḥ saṃviśati kramāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Worshipping during the two periods of junctions (the dawn and the dusk), and repeating the Sāman, Ṛk and Yajus hymns, the Brāhmaṇas propitiate and strengthen Rudra of the past and the future. At the time of rising, the sun stands on the Ṛks, at midday he stands on the Yajus and in the late afternoon, Rudra lies down and takes rest gradually. Hence, in fact, the sun never rises nor does he set.

## \|\| 1.10.27 \|\|

*tasmādbhavennābhyudito bāhyastamita eva ca \|*  
*na rudramprati meheta sarvāvasthaṃ kathaṃ cana \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. One shall never pass urine in the direction of Rudra (i.e. the sun) in whatever condition he may be.

## \|\| 1.10.28 \|\|

*evaṃ yuktān dvijān devo rudrastānna hinasti vai \|*  
*tato 'pravītpunarbrahmā taṃ devaṃ nīlalohitam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. Lord Rudra does not oppress the Brāhmaṇa who strictly adheres to these principles. Then Brahmā said again to that lord Nīlalohita.

## \|\| 1.10.29 \|\|

*dvitīyaṃ nāmadheyaṃ te mayā proktaṃ bhaveti yat \|*  
*etasyāpo dvitīyā te tanurnāmnā bhavatviti \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Your second name has been mentioned by me as Bhava. Let ṭhe waters be the second physical body of this name of yours.

## \|\| 1.10.30 \|\|

*ityukte tvatha tasyāsīccharīrasthaṃ rasātmakam \|*  
*viveśa tattadā yastu tasmādāpo bhavaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. On this being mentioned, the element of the nature of Rasa (Juice)(i.e. water) became stationed in his body. Since he entered it, the water is remembered as Bhava.

## \|\| 1.10.31 \|\|

*yasmādbhavanti bhūtāni tābhyastā bhāvayanti ca \|*  
*bhavanādrāvanāccaiva bhūtānāmucyate bhavaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. Since the living beings are born (bhavanāt) of him, and since he evolves (bhāvanāt) the living beings through them (i.e. the waters) he is called Bhava (due to his creation and evolution of beings).

## \|\| 1.10.32 \|\|

*tasmānmūtraṃ purīṣaṃ ca nāpsu kurvīta karhicit \|*  
*na niṣṭhīvennāvagāhennaiva gacchecca maithunam \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Hence, one shall never urinate or pass faeces into the waters. One should not spit into water, nor plunge into the water in the nude nor should anyone have sexual intercourse within the waters.

## \|\| 1.10.33 \|\|

*na caitāḥ paricakṣīta vahantyo vā sthitā api \|*  
*maidhyāmedhyāstvapāmetāstanavo munibhiḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. Nor should one enumerate (?) these whether flowing or still. These bodies of the waters are declared by the sages as Medhya (Pure) and Amedhya (Impure).

## \|\| 1.10.34 \|\|

*vivarṇarasagandhāśca varjyā alpāśca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*apāṃ yoniḥ samudrastu tasmāttaṃ kāmayanti tāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Waters devoid of taste, waters of bad odour and colour and water in very little quantity should be avoided on all occasions. The sea is the source of origin of waters. Hence waters desire it.

## \|\| 1.10.35 \|\|

*madhyāścaivāmṛtā hyāpo bhavanti prāpya sāgaram \|*  
*tasmādapo na rundhīta samudraṃ kāmayanti tāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. After reaching the sea, the waters become sacred and Amṛta (nectarine). Hence one should not obstruct the waters since they love the sea.

## \|\| 1.10.36 \|\|

*na hinasti bhavo devo ya evaṃ hyapsu vartate \|*  
*tato 'bravītpunarbrahmā kumāraṃ nīlalohitam \|\| 36 \|\|*

36a. Lord Bhava does not oppress or injure him who treats water thus.

36b. Then Brahmā said again to child Nīlalohita:

## \|\| 1.10.37 \|\|

*śarveti yattṛtīyaṃ te nāma proktaṃ mayā vibho \|*  
*tasya bhūmistṛtīyasya tanurnāmnā bhavattviyam \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. “O lord, the third name of yours that had been mentioned by me is Śarva. Let this earth be the physical body of that third name.

## \|\| 1.10.38 \|\|

*ityukte yatsthiraṃ tasya śarīre hyasthisaṃjñitam \|*  
*viveśa tattadā bhūmiṃ yasmātsā śarva ucyate \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. On this being mentioned, the hard and firm (part) in his body, namely bones entered the earth. Therefore, it is called Śarva.

## \|\| 1.10.39 \|\|

*tasmātkṛṣṭena kurvīta purīṣaṃ mūtrameva ca \|*  
*na cchāyāyāṃ tathā mārge svacchāyāyāṃ na mehayet \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Hence, one should not evacuate the bowels or- urinate in the ploughed land. One should not urinate in the shade of trees, or in the pathway or in one’s own shadow.

## \|\| 1.10.40 \|\|

*śiraḥ prāvṛtya kurvīta antardhāya tṛṇairmahīm \|*  
*evaṃ yo vartate bhūmau śarvastaṃ na hinasti vai \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. After covering the ground with grass and covering one’s head, one should evacute the bowels. Śarva does not oppress or injure him who behaves like this towards the earth.

## \|\| 1.10.41-43 \|\|

*tato 'bravītpunarbrahmā kumāraṃ nīlalohitam \|*  
*īśāneti caturtha te nāma proktaṃ mayeha yat \|\| 41 \|\|*

*caturthasya caturthī tu vāyurnāmnā tanustava \|*  
*ityukte yaccharīrasthaṃ pañcadhā prāṇasaṃjñitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

*viveśa tasya tadvāyumīśānastana mārutaḥ \|*  
*tasmānnainaṃ parivadetpravāntaṃ vāyumīśvaram \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. Then Brahmā said again to child Nīlalohita. “Your fourth name that had been declared by me is Īśāna. Vāyu (Wind) should be the fourth physical body of your fourth name. As soon as this was spoken that (vital breath) which was stationed in him in five groups and is termed Prāṇa (Vital breath) entered Vāyu. Hence wind is Īśāna. Hence one should not censure or revile at Vāyu the lord himself as it blows violently.

## \|\| 1.10.44 \|\|

*yajñairvyavaharantyenaṃ ye vai paricaranti ca \|*  
*evaṃ yuktaṃ maheśāno naiva devo hinasti tam \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Lord Maheśāna does not oppress or injure him who properly behaves towards the wind and those who honour the wind by means of Yajñas and those who serve it.

## \|\| 1.10.45-49 \|\|

*tato 'bravītpunarbrahmā taṃ devaṃ dha5mlamīśvaram \|*  
*nāma yadvai paśupatirityuktaṃ pañcamaṃ mayā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*pañcamī pañcama syaiṣā tanurnāmnāgnirastu te \|*  
*ityukte yaccharīrasthaṃ tejastasyoṣṇasaṃjñitam \|\| 46 \|\|*

*viveśa tattadā hyagniṃ tasmātpaśupatistu saḥ \|*  
*yasmādagniḥ paśuścāsīdyasmātpāti paśūṃśca saḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tasmātpaśupatestasya tanuragnirnirucyate \|*  
*tasmādamedyaṃ na dahenna ca pādau pratāpayet \|\| 48 \|\|*

*adhastānnopadadhyācca na cainamatilaṅghayet \|*  
*nainaṃ paśupatirdeva evaṃ yuktaṃ hinasti vai \|\| 49 \|\|*

45-49. Then Brahmā said again to that lord Dhūmra (smoke-coloured) Īśvara. “The fifth name of yours that had been mentioned by me is Paśupati. Let this Agni (Fire) be the fifth body of your fifth name”. On this being mentioned, the fiery brilliance that had been stationed in his body and is termed Uṣṇa (Hot) entered the fire. Hence it (fire) is Paśupati. Since Agni is Paśu (Animal) and since he protects animals, the physical body of Paśupati is designated (defined) as Agni. Hence, one should not burn impure ordure nor should one warm one’s feet. One should not place it beneath nor should one trespass it. Lord Paśupati does not oppress or injure him who behaves properly like this.

## \|\| 1.10.50-54 \|\|

*tato 'bravītpunarbrahmā taṃ devaṃ śvetapiṅgalam \|*  
*ṣaṣṭaṃ nāma mayā proktaṃ tava bhīmeti yatprabho \|\| 50 \|\|*

*ākāśaṃ tasya nāmnastu tanuḥ ṣaṣṭhī bhavatviti \|*  
*ityukte suṣiraṃ tasya śarīrasthamabhūcca yat \|\| 51 \|\|*

*viveśa tattadākāśaṃ tasmādbhīmasya sā tanuḥ \|*  
*yadākāśe smṛto devastasmānnā saṃvṛtaḥ kvacit \|\| 52 \|\|*

*kuryānmūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā na bhuñjīta pibenna vā \|*  
*maithunaṃ vāpi na careducchiṣṭāni ca notkṣipet \|\| 53 \|\|*

*na hinasti ca taṃ devo yo bhīme hyevamācaret \|*  
*tato 'bravītpunarbrahmā taṃ devaṃ sabalaṃ prabhum \|\| 54 \|\|*

50-54. Then Brahmā said once again to that lord Śvetapiṅgala (White-and-tawny-coloured). “O lord, the sixth name of yours that had been mentioned by me is Bhīma. Let Ākāśa (Ether) be the sixth body of that name”. On this being uttered, the cavity that had been in his body entered the ether. Hence, it is the body of Bhīma. Since the lord is remembered as existing in the ether. One should not evacuate the bowels, urinate, take food, drink water, have sexual intercourse or throw up leavings of food consumed without having a cover on. The lord does not oppress or injure him who behaves towards Bhīma thus. Then Brahmā said once again to that lord, who is mighty.

## \|\| 1.10.55 \|\|

*saptamaṃ yanmayā proktaṃ nāmogreti tava prabho \|*  
*tasya nāmnastanustubhyaṃ dvijo bhavati dīkṣitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. O lord, your seventh name that had been mentioned by me was Ugra. The initiated Brāhmaṇa becomes the body of that name of yours.

## \|\| 1.10.56 \|\|

*evamukte tu yattasya caitanyaṃ vai śarīragam \|*  
*viveśa dīkṣitaṃ tadvai brāhmaṇaṃ somayājinam \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. On this being uttered, the Caitanya (consciousness, alertness) that was in his body entered the initiated Brāhmaṇa who performs the Soma sacrifice.

## \|\| 1.10.57 \|\|

*tāvatkālaṃ smṛto vipra ugro devastu dīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*tasmānnemaṃ parivadennāślīlaṃ cāsya kīrttayet \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. For that duration, the initiated Brāhmaṇa becomes lord Ugra. Hence, no one shall abuse or revile at him nor shall anyone speak vulgar words about him.

## \|\| 1.10.58 \|\|

*te harantyasya pāpmānaṃ ye vai parivadanti tam \|*  
*evaṃ yuktān dvijānugro devastānna hinasti vai \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. Those who censure him take away his sins. Lord Ugra does not oppress or injure those Brāhmaṇas who behave properly thus.

## \|\| 1.10.59-61 \|\|

*tatobravītpunarbrahmā taṃ devaṃ bhāskaradyutim \|*  
*aṣṭamaṃ nāma yat proktaṃ mahādeveti te mayā \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tasya nāmno 'ṣṭamasyāstu tanustubhyaṃ tu candramāḥ \|*  
*ityukte yanmana stasya saṃkalpakamabhūtprabhoḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*viveśa taccandramasaṃ mahādevastataḥ śaśī \|*  
*tasmādvibhāvyate hyeṣa mahādevastu candramāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

59-61. Then Brahmā once again said to that lord with the lustre of the sun, “Your eight name that had been men-

tioned by me is Mahādeva. Let the moon be the physical body of that eighth name of yours”. On this being mentioned, the mind of the lord that had been conceiving and contemplating entered the Candramasa (Moon). Therefore, the moon, is Mahādeva. Hence, this great lord is considered to be the Moon.

## \|\| 1.10.62 \|\|

*amāvāsyāṃ na vai chindyādvṛkṣagulmauṣadhīrdvijaḥ \|*  
*mahādevaḥ smṛtaḥ somastasyātmā hyauṣadhīgaṇaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. On the new moon day a Brāhmaṇa should not cut trees, bushes or medicinal herbs. Soma (Moon) is remembered as Mahādeva and his Ātman (soul) is the group of medicinal herbs.

## \|\| 1.10.63-65 \|\|

*evaṃ yo varttate caiha sadā parvaṇi parvaṇi \|*  
*na hanti taṃ mahādevo ya evaṃ veda taṃ prabhum \|\| 63 \|\|*

*gopāyati divādityaḥ prajā naktaṃ tu candramāḥ \|*  
*ekarātrau sameyātāṃ sūryā candramasāvubhau \|\| 64 \|\|*

*amāvāsyāniśāyāṃ tu tasyāṃ yuktaḥ sādā bhavet \|*  
*rudrāviṣṭaṃ sarvamidaṃ tanubhirnnāmabhiśca ha \|\| 65 \|\|*

63-65. Mahādeva does not slay him who always remains thus on the Parvan days (new moon, full moon etc.) and who understands that lord thus.

The sun protects the subjects by the day and the moon, at the night. On the night (i.e. on the new moon) the sun and the moon join together. On that Amāvāsyā (New Moon) night one shall always be Yukta (properly performing Yogic exercise). All this visible universe has been pervaded by Rudra, through his bodies and names.

## \|\| 1.10.66 \|\|

*ekākī caścaratyeṣa sūryo 'sau rudra ucyate \|*  
*sūryasya yatprakāśena vīkṣante cakṣuṣā prajāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. This sun that wanders alone is called Rudra. It is due to the light of the sun that the subjects see with their eyes.

## \|\| 1.10.67-69 \|\|

*muktātmā saṃsthito rudraḥ pibatyaṃbho gabhastibhiḥ \|*  
*adyate pīyate caiva hyannapānādikāmyayā \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tanuraṃbūdbhavā sā vai deheṣvevopacīyate \|*  
*yayā dhatte prajāḥ sarvāḥ sthirībhūtena tejasā \|\| 68 \|\|*

*pārthivī sā tanustasya sādhvī dhārayate prajāḥ \|*  
*yā ca sthitā śarīreṣu bhūtānāṃ prāṇavṛttibhiḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

67-69. Rudra remains a liberated soul and drinks water through his rays. Food is eaten and water is drunk with a desire for food, water etc. The body arising out of water develops and nourishes the bodies.

That earthen body of the lord is good as it sustains the subjects. It is through this that the lord upholds all the subjects by means of a steady splendour.

## \|\| 1.10.70-75 \|\|

*vātātmikā tu caiśānī sā prāṇaḥ prāṇināmiha \|*  
*pītāśitāni pacati bhūtānāṃ jaṭhareṣviha \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tanuḥ pāśupatī tasya pācakaḥ so 'gnirucyate \|*  
*yānīha śuṣirāṇi syurdeheṣvantargatāni vai \|\| 71 \|\|*

*vāyoḥ saṃcaraṇārthāni bhīmā sā procyate tanuḥ \|*  
*vaitānyādīkṣitānāṃ tu yā sthitirbrahmavādinām \|\| 72 \|\|*

*tanurugrātmikā sā tu tenogro dīkṣitaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*yattu saṃkalpakaṃ tasya prajāsviha samāsthitam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*sā tanurmānasī tasya candramāḥ prāṇiṣu sthitaḥ \|*  
*navonavo yo bhavati jāyamānaḥ punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*pīyate 'sau yathākālaṃ vibudhaiḥ pitṛbhiḥ saha \|*  
*mahādevo 'mṛtātmā sa candramā ammayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

70-75. The gaseous body of Īśāna is the vital breath of all living beings. It is stationed in the bodies of all living beings along with the functions of the vital breath.

The body of Paśupati cooks and digests the food consumed and the beverages drunk, in the bellies of the living beings. That which cooks is called Agni (fire i.e. Gastric fire).

The cavities that are within the bodies for the purpose of the free movement of the air constitute the body (of the lord) called Bhīma.

The existence of expounders of Brahman is, due to Caitanya (consciousness) of the initiated ones. That body is of the form of Ugra. Therefore, the initiated one is remembered as Ugra.

The part of the body that conceives and contemplates and which is stationed in the subjects is the mental body, the moon—it is stationed in the living beings. Being born again and again he becomes fresh and fresh. It is being drunk at the proper time by the Devas along with the Pitṛs. The moon of aquatic nature with nectar within him is remembered as Mahādeva.

## \|\| 1.10.76 \|\|

*tasya yā prathamā nāmnā tanū raudrī prakīrttitā \|*  
*patnī suvarccalā tasyāḥ putraścāsya śanaiścaraḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. His first body has been glorified by the name Rauḍrī. Its wife is Suvarcalā and her son is Śanaiścara (the Saturn).

## \|\| 1.10.77 \|\|

*bhavasya yā dvitīyā tu āpo nāmnā tanuḥ smṛtā \|*  
*tasyā dhātrī smṛtā patnī putraśca uśanā smṛtaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

77\. The second body of Bhava is remembered by the name of Āpaḥ. Its wife is remembered as Dhātrī and the son is remembered as Uśanas (the Venus).

## \|\| 1.10.78 \|\|

*śarvasya yā tṛtīyasya nāmno bhūmistanuḥ smṛtā \|*  
*tasyāḥ patnī vikeśī tu putro 'syāṅgārakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

78\. The body of the third name of Śarva is Bhūmī (the earth). Its wife is Vikeśī and the son is remembered as Aṅgāraka (the Mars).

## \|\| 1.10.79-84 \|\|

*īśānasya caturthasya nāmnā vātastanustu yā \|*  
*tasyāḥ patnī śivā nāma putraścāsyā manojavaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*avijñātagatiścaiva dvau putrau cānilasya tu \|*  
*nāmnā paśupateryā tu tanuragnirdvijaiḥ smṛtā \|\| 80 \|\|*

*tasyāḥ patnī smṛtā svāhā skandastasyāḥ sutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*nāmnā ṣaṣṭhasya yā bhīmā tanurākāśamucyate \|\| 81 \|\|*

*diśaḥ patnyaḥ smṛtāstasya svargaścāpi sutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*agrā tanuḥ saptamī yā dīkṣito brāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*dīkṣā patnī smṛtā tasyāḥ saṃtānaḥ putra ucyate \|*  
*nāmnāṣṭamasya mahastanuryā candramāḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*tasya vai rohiṇī patnī putrastasya budhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*ityetāstanavastasya nāmabhiḥ saha kīrtitāḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

79-84. Vāta (wind) is the body of the fourth name of Īśāna. Its wife is Śivā by name. Anila (Wind) has two sons, viz.: Manojava (Having the speed of the mind) and Avijñātagati (One of inscrutable movement).

Agni (Fire) is remembered by Brāhmaṇas, as the body of Paśupati. Svāhā is remembered as its wife. Skanda is remembered as its son.

The Ether (Ākāśa) is called the body Bhīma, his sixth name. The quarters are remembered as its wives and Svarga (heaven) is remembered as its son.

The seventh body Ugra is remembered as the initiated Brāhmaṇa. Dīkṣā is remembered as its wife and Santana is called the son.

The body Mahat of the eighth name is remembered as Candramas (Moon). Its wife is Rohiṇī. Her son is remembered as Budha.

Thus these bodies of his have been recounted along with the names.

## \|\| 1.10.85-87 \|\|

*tāsu vandyo namasyaśca pratināmatanūṣu vai \|*  
*sūryepsūrvyāṃ tathā vāyāvagnau vyomnyatha dīkṣite \|\| 85 \|\|*

*bhaktaistathā candramasi bhattayā vandyastu nāmabhiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ yo vetti taṃ devaṃ tanubhirnāmabhiśca ha \|\| 86 \|\|*

*prajāvāneti sāyujyamīśvarasya bhavasya saḥ \|*  
*ityetadvo mayā proktaṃ guhyaṃ bhīmāsya yadyaśaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

85-87. The lord is to be saluted and bowed to in those bodies with the respective names for each body. He should be saluted by devotees in the sun, the waters, the Earth, the wind, the fire, the Ether, the initiated one as well as the moon. He should be honoured with great devotion along with the names. He who knows that lord thus with the bodies and names acquires progeny and attains the Sāyujya (Identity) of Lord Bhava. Thus the esoteric fame of Bhīma has been recounted to you.

## \|\| 1.10.88 \|\|

*śanno 'stu dvipade viprāḥ śanno 'stu ca catuṣpade \|*  
*etatproktamidānīṃ ca tanūnāṃ nāmabhi saha \|*  
*mahādevasya devasya bhṛgostu śṛṇuta prajāḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

88\. O Brāhmaṇas, let there be welfare unto the bipeds. Let there be welfare unto the quadrupeds. Now the names and bodies of Mahādeva have been recounted. Listen to the progeny of Bhṛgu.

## Chapter 11 - The creation of Sages (saptarṣi)

## \|\| 1.11.1-3 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*bhṛgoḥ khyātirvijajñe vai īśvarau sukhaduḥkhayoḥ \|*  
*śubhāśubhapradātārau sarvaprāṇabhṛtāmiha \|\| 1 \|\|*

*devau dhātṛvidhātārau manvantaravicāriṇau \|*  
*tayārjyeṣṭhā tu bhaginī devī śrīrlokabhāvinī \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sā tu nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ pati māsadya śobhanā \|*  
*nārāyaṇātmajau tasyāṃ balonmādauvyajāyatām \|\| 3 \|\|*

Notes: This chapter deals with the progeny of the famous seven sages such as Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Atri, Pulaha and others. After mentioning their important descendants we are told that all these races passed away in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara. This chapter corresponds to Vā.P.ch.28.

Sūta said:

1-3. Khyāti gave birth to a daugher and two sons. The sons were masters of happiness and misery. They grant auspicious and inauspicious results unto all living beings. They were the gods Dhātṛ (supporter) and Vidhātṛ (Dispenser of destiny). They used (to live and) walkabout throughout the Manvantara. Their elder sister, goddess Śrī, purified the worlds. The splendid lady attained lord Nārāyaṇa as her husband. Bala (strength) and Unmāda (lunacy) were born of her as the sons of Nārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 1.11.4-6 \|\|

*balasya tejaḥ putrastu unmādasya tu saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*tasyānye mānasāḥ putrā āsan vyomavicāriṇaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ye vahanti vimānāni devānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām \|*  
*merukalpe smṛte bhārye vidhāturdhātureva ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*āyatirniyatiścaiva tayoḥ putrau dṛḍhavratau \|*  
*prāṇaścaiva mṛkaṇḍaśca brahmakośau sanātanau \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-5a. Tejas (fiery brilliance) was the son of Bala and Saṃśaya (Doubt) was the son of Unmāda. Other mental sons too were born of him. They move about in the firmament. They drive and carry the aerial chariots of the Devas and persons of auspicious rites.

5b-6. Āyati (future) and Niyati (Restraint), the daughters of Meru are remembered as the wives of Vidhātṛ and Dhātṛ. Prāṇa and Mṛkaṇḍa of firm holy vows were their sons. They are eternal and Brahmakośas (the treasury of Brahman or Vedas).

## \|\| 1.11.7 \|\|

*manasvinyāṃ mṛkaṇḍasya mārkaṇḍeyo babhūva ha \|*  
*suto vedaśirāstasya dhūmrapatnyāmajāyata \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Mārkaṇḍeya was born of Manasvinī (as the son) of Mṛkaṇḍa. His son Vedaśiras was born of Dhūmrapatnī.

## \|\| 1.11.8 \|\|

*pīvaryāṃ vedaśirasaḥ putrā vaśakarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyāḥ samākhyātā ṛṣayo vedapāragāḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Sons of Vedaśiras in (through) Pīvarī are remembered as Propagators of the race. These sages who are well-known as Mārkaṇḍeyas (Descendants of Mṛkaṇḍa) were masters of the Vedas.

## \|\| 1.11.9-10 \|\|

*prāṇasya puṇḍarīkāyāṃ dyutimānātmajo 'bhavat \|*  
*unnataścadyutimataḥ svanavātaśca tāvubhau \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tayoḥ putrāśca pautrāśca bhārgavāṇāṃ parasparāt \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuventare 'tītā marīceḥ śṛṇuta prajāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Dyutimān was born of Puṇḍarīkā, as the son of Prāṇa. Dyutimān had two sons, viz.: Unnata and Svanavāta. These two sons had sons and grandsons through mutual alliances among the descendants of Bhṛgu. They passed away during the Svāyambhuva Manvantara.

Listen to the progeny of Marīci.

## \|\| 1.11.11 \|\|

*patnī marīceḥ saṃbhūtirvijajñe hyātmasaṃbhaṃvam \|*  
*prajāpateḥ pūrṇamāsaṃ kanyāścemā nibodhata \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Understand that, Sambhūti, the wife of Marīci the Prajāpati, gave birth to the son Pūrṇamāsa and the following daughters:

## \|\| 1.11.12 \|\|

*kṛṣirvṛṣṭistviṣā caiva tathā copacitiḥ śubhā \|*  
*pūrṇamāsaḥ sarasvatyāṃ putrau dvāvudapādayat \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. Kṛṣi, Vṛṣṭi, Tviṣā and the splendid Upaciti. Pūrṇamāsa begot of Sarasvatī two sons:

## \|\| 1.11.13 \|\|

*virajaṃ caiva dharmiṣṭhaṃ parvaśaṃ caiva tāvubhau \|*  
*virajasyātmajo vidvān sudhāmā nāma viśrutaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The two were Viraja who was righteous and Paravaśa. Viraja’s son was a scholar, well known by the name Sudhāman.

## \|\| 1.11.14 \|\|

*sudhāmā sa tu vairājaḥ prācīṃ diśamupā śritaḥ \|*  
*lokapālaḥ sa dharmātmā gaurīputraḥ pratāpavān \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Sudhāman, the son of Viraja and Gaurī, resorted to the Eastern quarter. He was a valorous and noble-souled guardian of the quarter, (ruler of the world).

## \|\| 1.11.15-16 \|\|

*parvaśaḥ parvagaṇanāṃ praviṣṭaḥ sa mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*parvaśaḥ parvaśāyāṃ tu janayā māsa vai sutau \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yajurdhāma ca dhīmantaṃ staṃbhakāśyapameva ca \|*  
*tayorgotrakarau putrau jātau saṃnyāsaniścitau \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. Parvaśa, of great fame, entered (the task of) counting holy occasions (Parva-gaṇana?). Parvaśa begot of Parvaśā two sons, viz.: Yajurdhāman the intelligent and Stambhakāśyapa. Their two sons Sanyāsa and Niścita stabilised their line.

## \|\| 1.11.17-18 \|\|

*smṛtastvaṃ girasaḥ patnī jajñe sā hyātmasaṃbhavān \|*  
*putro kanyāścatasraśca puṇyāstā lokaviśrutāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sinīvālī kuhūścaiva rākā cānumatistathā \|*  
*tathaiva bharatāgniṃ ca kīrtimantaṃ ca tāvubhau \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Smṛti, the wife of Aṅgiras, gave birth to these children—four daughters and two sons. The four daughters who were holy and well-reputed in the worlds, were viz. Sinīvālī, Kuhū, Rākā and Anumati. The two sons were Bharatāgni and Kīrtimān.

## \|\| 1.11.19 \|\|

*agneḥ putraṃ ca parjanyaṃ sadvatī suṣuve tathā \|*  
*hiraṇyaromā parjanyo mārīcyāmudapadyata \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Sadvatī gave birth to Parjanya the son of Agni (i.e. Bharatāgni). (Another) Parjanya (otherwise called) Hir-aṇyaroman was born of Marīci.

## \|\| 1.11.20-21 \|\|

*ābhūtasaṃplavasthāyī lokapālaḥ sa vai smṛtaḥ \|*  
*yajñe kīrttimataścāpi dhenukā vītakalmaṣau \|\| 20 \|\|*

*cariṣṇuṃ dhṛtimantaṃ ca ubhāvaṅgirasāṃ varau \|*  
*tayoḥ putrāśca pautrāśca atītā vai sahasraśaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. He is remembered as a Lokapāla (ruler of the world, guardian of the quarter) staying till the ultimate deluge.

Dhenuka gave birth to Cariṣṇu and Dhṛtimān, the two sinless sons of Kīrtimān. Both of them were the most excellent among the descendants of Aṅgiras. Their sons and grandsons ran to thousands. They have all passed away.

## \|\| 1.11.22-24 \|\|

*anasūyā vijajñe vai pañcātreyānakalmaṣān \|*  
*kanyāṃ caiva śrutiṃ nāma mātā śaṅkhapadasya sā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kardasasya tu patnī sā paulahasya prajāpateḥ \|*  
*satyanetraśca havyaśca āpo mūrttiḥ śanaiścaraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*somaśca pañcamasteṣāmāsītsvāyaṃbhuventare \|*  
*yāmadevaissahātītāḥ pañcātreyāḥ prakīrttitāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. Anasūyā gave birth to five Ātreyas (i.e. sons of Atri) who were free from sins. She gave birth to a daughter also named Śruti who was the mother of Śaṅkhapāda. She was the wife of Kardama, the Prajāpati (Lord of subjects) and son of Pulaha. The five Ātreyas were Satya-Netra, Havya, Āpomūrti, Śanaiścara and Soma the fifth one among them. They passed away along with the Yāmadevas in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara.

## \|\| 1.11.25 \|\|

*teṣāṃ putrāśca pautrāśca ātreyāṇāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare 'tītāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The sons and grandsons of those noble-souled Ātreyas were hundreds and thousands. They all passed away in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara.

## \|\| 1.11.26 \|\|

*prītyāṃ pulastyabhāryāyāṃ dānā gnistatsuto 'bhavat \|*  
*pūrvajanmani so 'gastyaḥ smṛtaḥ svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Dānāgni was the son of Prīti, the wife of Pulastya. He is remembered as Agastya in his previous birth in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara.

## \|\| 1.11.27-29 \|\|

*madhyamo devabāhuśca atrināmā ca te trayaḥ \|*  
*svamā yavīyasī teṣāṃ sadvatī nāma viśrutā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*parjanyajananī śubhrā patnī cāgneḥ smṛtā śubhā \|*  
*paulastyasya ca brahmarṣeḥ prītiputrasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*dānācca suṣuve patnī sujaṅghī caṃ bahūnsutān \|*  
*paulastyā iti vikhyātāḥ smṛtāḥ svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare \|\| 29 \|\|*

27-28a. The middle one was Devabāhu and the third son was Atri by name (thus Pulastya had) three sons. Their younger sister named Sadvatī was well-known. She is remembered as the splendid and pure wife of Agni (i.e. Bharatāgni) and mother of Parjanya.

28b-29. Sujaṅghī, the wife of Dānāgni, the intelligent son of the Brahmanical sage Pulastya and Prīti, gave birth to many sons. They are well known as Paulastyas. They are remembered (to have lived) in Svāyambhuva Manvantara.

## \|\| 1.11.30 \|\|

*kṣamā tu suṣuve putrānpulastyasya prajāpateḥ \|*  
*tretāgnivarcasaḥ sarve yeṣāṃ kīrttiḥ pratiṣṭhitā \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Kṣamā gave birth to the sons of Pulaha, the Prajāpati. All of them had the brilliance of the three sacrificial fires. Their fame is well-established.

## \|\| 1.11.31 \|\|

*kardamaścorvarīvāṃśca sahiṣṇuśceti te trayaḥ \|*  
*ṛṣiḥ kanakapīṭhaśca śubhā kanyā ca pīvarī \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. They were three viz. Kardama, Urvarivān and Sahiṣṇu. Sage Kanakapīṭha (also was his son). There was a beautiful daughter named Pīvarī.

## \|\| 1.11.32 \|\|

*kardamasya śrutiḥ patnī ātreyyajanayatsvayam \|*  
*putraṃ śaṅkhapadaṃ nāma kanyāṃ kāmyāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Karḍama’s wife Śruti who was the daughter of Atri gave birth to a son named Śaṅkhapāda and a daughter named Kāmyā.

## \|\| 1.11.33 \|\|

*sa vai śaṅkhapadaḥ śrīmāṃllokapālaḥ prajāpatiḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi rataḥ kāmyā dattā priyavrate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. It is reported that this Śaṅkhapāda was prosperous ruler of the world and lord of the subjects. He was devoted to the southern quarter.

Kāmyā was given in marriage to Priyavrata.

## \|\| 1.11.34 \|\|

*kāmyā priyavratāllebhe svāyaṃbhuvasamānsutān \|*  
*daśa kanyādvayaṃ caiva yaiḥ kṣatraṃ sampravarttitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Kāmyā bore to Priyavrata ten sons on a par with the Svāyambhuva Manu and two daughters. It is through these that the Kṣatriya race spread.

## \|\| 1.11.35 \|\|

*putraṃ kanakapīṭhasya sahiṣṇuṃ nāma viśrutam \|*  
*yaśodharā vijajñe vai kāmadevaṃ sumadhyāmā \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. Yaśodharā, the lady of beautiful waist, gave birth to Sahiṣṇu, the son of Kanakapīṭha. (She gave birth) to Kāmadeva (also).

## \|\| 1.11.36 \|\|

*kratoḥ kratusamānpu trān vijajñe saṃnatiḥ śubhān \|*  
*teṣāṃ na bhāryā putro vā sarve te urddharetasaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Sannati bore auspicious sons to Kratu. They were equal to Kratu. They had neither wives nor sons. All of them were celibate.

## \|\| 1.11.37 \|\|

*tāni ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi vālakhilyā iti śrutāḥ \|*  
*aruṇasyāgrato yānti parivārya divākaram \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. They were well known as Vālakhilyas and are sixty thousand in number. They surround the sun and go ahead in front of Aruṇa.

## \|\| 1.11.38-40 \|\|

*ābhūtasaṃplavātsarvepataṅgasahacāriṇaḥ \|*  
*svasārau tadyavīyasyau puṇyā satyavatī cate \|\| 38 \|\|*

*parvaśasya snuve te vai pūrṇamāsa sutasya tu \|*  
*ūrjāyāṃ tu vasiṣṭhasya vāsiṣṭhāḥ sapta jajñire \|\| 39 \|\|*

*jyāyasī ca sutā teṣāṃ puṇḍarīkā sumadhyamā \|*  
*jananī sā dyutimataḥ prāṇasya mahiṣī priyāḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-39a. All of them are (perpetual) associates of the Sun till the time of ultimate annihilation (of the universe). They had two younger sisters, Puṇyā and Satyavatī. They were the daughters-in-law of Parvaśā, the son of Pūrṇamāsa.

39b-40. The seven (Vasiṣṭhas) were born of Ūrjā as the sons of Vasiṣṭha. Their elder sister was a daughter of beautiful waist named Puṇḍarīkā. She was the mother of Dyutimān and the beloved wife of Prāṇa.

## \|\| 1.11.41-44 \|\|

*tasyāstu ye yavīyāṃso vāsiṣṭhāḥ sapta viśrutāḥ \|*  
*rakṣo garttorddhabā huśca savanaḥ pavanaśca yaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*sutapāḥ saṃkurityete sarve saptarṣayaḥ samṛtāḥ \|*  
*ratno varāṅgyajanayanmārkaṇḍeyī yaśasvinī \|\| 42 \|\|*

*pratīcyāṃ diśi rājānaṃ ketumantaṃ prajāpatim \|*  
*gotrāṇi nāmabhisteṣāṃ vāsiṣṭhānāṃ mahātmanām \|\| 43 \|\|*

*svāyaṃbhuve 'ntaretītānyagnestu śṛṇuta prajāḥ \|*  
*ityeṣa ṛṣisargastu sānubandhaḥ prakīrttitaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

41-42a. Her younger brothers, the seven sons of Vasiṣṭha are well known. They are—Rakṣa, Garta, Ūrdhvabāhu, Savana, Pavana, Sutapas and Śaṅku. All of them are remembered as seven sages.

42b-44. The famous daughter of Mārkaṇḍeya, the noble lady of excellent limbs, gave birth to Ratna, the king of western quarter. (He was also known as) Ketumān and he was a Prajāpati. The races of the noble-souled sons of Vasiṣṭha passed away in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara.

Listen to the progeny of Agni.

Thus the creation of sages has been recounted along with their attendants. Henceforth, I shall recount the family of Agni in detail and in the proper order.

## Chapter 12 - The race of Agni

## \|\| 1.12.2-3 \|\|

*pāvakaṃ pavamānaṃ ca śuciragniśca yaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*nirmathyaḥ pavamānastu vaidyutaḥ pāvakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śuciḥ saurastu vijñeyaḥ svāhāputrāstu te trayaḥ \|*  
*nirmathyaḥ pavamānastu śuciḥ saurastu yaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

Notes: This chapter presents the forty-nine ritualistic functions of the Fire as so many different Agni gods and gives their arrangement or correlations in a genealogical form. As a matter of fact, it is a Vedic concept as can be seen from the notes. This section concerning Agnivaṃśa must have been possibly a part of the original (Ur-) purāṇa as many verses hereof are textually identical with those in Vā.P. 29, Mt.P.51. The Mbh. Vana Chs. 217-22 (Āṅgirasa upākhyāna) give a detailed description of the ritualistic functions of fire.

l-2a. A mental son of Brahmā is remembered as the deity identifying itself with fire in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara. Svāhā bore to him three sons, viz.: Pavamāna and Śuci who is remembered as Agni also.

2b-3. The Pavamāna fire is that which is obtained by churning (the Araṇi), Pāvaka is the fire originating from lightning. Śuci should be known as the solar fire. These are the three sons of Svāhā. \[(Repetition) the Pavamāna fire is that which is obtained by churning (the Araṇi), and Śuci is remembered as solar fire.\]

## \|\| 1.12.4-6 \|\|

*abyonirvaidyutaścaiva teṣāṃ sthānāni tāni vai \|*  
*pavamānātmajaścaiva kavyavāhana ucyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*pāvakiḥ saharakṣastu havyavāhaḥ śuceḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*devānāṃ havyavāho 'gniḥ pitṝṇāṃ kavyavāhanaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*saha rakṣo 'surāṇāṃ tu trayāṇāṃ tu trayo 'gnayaḥ \|*  
*eteṣāṃ putrapautrāstu catvāriṃśanna vaiva tu \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. The Pāvaka fire has water as the source of origin and it originates from the lightning. They are their respective abodes (viz.: Araṇi, the sun and the lightning). Kavyavāhana is said to be the son of Pavamāna. Saharakṣa was the son of Pāvaka and Havyavāha was the son of Śuci.

Havyavāha is the fire of the Devas; Kavyavāhana is the fire of the Pitṛs; Saharakṣa is the fire of the Asuras. There are (thus) three fires pertaining to the three (i.e. the Devas, the Pitṛs and the Asuras). The sons and grandsons of these are forty-nine in number.

## \|\| 1.12.7 \|\|

*vakṣyāmi nāmabhisteṣāṃ pravibhāgaṃ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*viśrupto laukiko 'gnistu prathamo brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. I shall mention their divisions separately along with their names. The secular fire is well known as the first son of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.12.8 \|\|

*brahmo dattāgnisa tputro bharato nāma viśrutaḥ \|*  
*vaiśvānaraḥ sutastasya vahan havyaṃ samāḥ śatam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. The good son of Brahmadattāgni (the fire handed over by Brahmā) is well known by the name Bharata. Vaiśvānara was his son, and he carried Havya for a hundred years.

## \|\| 1.12.9-10 \|\|

*saṃbhṛto 'tharvaṇā pūrvamedhitiḥ puṣkarodadhau \|*  
*sotharvā laukiko 'gnistu darpahātharvaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*atharvā tu bhṛgurjajñe hyagnirātharvaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasmātsa laukiko 'gnistu dadhyaṅṅātharvaṇo mataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. Formerly the fire Edhiti was gathered by Atharvan in the ocean Puṣkara. Hence that secular fire is Ātharvaṇa. Darpahā is remembered as the son of Atharvan. Bhṛgu was born as Atharvan and Fire is remembered as Ātharvaṇa (son of Atharvan). Hence the secular fire is considered Dadhyaṅ, the son of Atharvaṇa.

## \|\| 1.12.11 \|\|

*ātharvaḥ pavamānastu nirmathyaḥ kavibhiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*sa jñeyo gārhapatyo 'gnistasya putradvayaṃ smṛtam \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Pavamāna, the son of Atharvan, is remembered by the wise as one that should be generated by churning. It should be known as Gārhapatya fire. His two sons are remembered as follows:

## \|\| 1.12.12 \|\|

*śaṃsyastvāha vanīyo 'gneḥ smṛto yo havyavāhanaḥ \|*  
*dvitīyastu sutaḥ proktaḥ śuko 'gniryaḥ praṇīyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. (They are Śaṃsya and Śuka (śukra in Vā.P. 9-11) Śaṃsya is Āhavanīya fire who is remembered as Havyavāhana. The second son is Śuka (śukra in Vā.P.) and he is said to be the fire that is gathered and carried.

## \|\| 1.12.13 \|\|

*tathā savyāpasavyau ca śaṃsyasyāgneḥ sutāvubhau \|*  
*śaṃsyastu ṣoḍaśa nadīścakame havyavāhanaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Savya and Apasavya were the two sons of Śaṃsya. Śaṃsya, the Havyavāhana, loved sixteen rivers.

## \|\| 1.12.14-18 \|\|

*yo sāvāhavanīyo 'gnirabhimānī dvijaiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*kāverīṃ kṛṣṇaveṇāṃ ca narmadāṃ yamunāṃ tathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*godāvarīṃ vitastāṃ ca candrabhāgāmirāvatīm \|*  
*vipāśāṃ kauśikīñcaiva śatadrūṃ sarayūṃ tathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sītāṃ sarasvatīṃ caiva hrādinīṃ pāvanīntathā \|*  
*tāsu ṣoḍaśadhāmānaṃ pravibhajya pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ātmānaṃ vyadadhāttāsu dhiṣṇīṣvatha babhūva saḥ \|*  
*kṛttikācāriṇī dhiṣṇī jajñire tāśca dhiṣṇayaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dhiṣṇīṣu jajñire yasmād dhiṣṇayastena kīrttitāḥ \|*  
*ityete vai nadīputrā dhiṣṇīṣvevaṃ vijajñire \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. The fire Śaṃsya who is remembered as Āhavanīya fire as well as one who is identified with fire (Abhimānin, one who takes pride) by the Brāhmaṇas loved these sixteen rivers: viz.: Kāverī, Kṛṣṇaveṇā, Narmadā, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Vitastā, Canḍrabhāgā, Irāvatī, Vipāśā, Kauśikī, Śatadru, Sarayū, Sītā, Sarasvatī, Hrādinī and Pāvanī. He divided himself into sixteen Dhāmans (abodes) and in those abodes he deposited himself. The Dhiṣṇīs (abodes i.e. fire-places) were caused to move by vehicles (Kṛttikas) (?) and the sons were born in those Dhiṣṇīs. Hence those sons are called “Dhiṣṇis”. Thus these sons of the rivers were born in the Dhiṣṇis and they are glorified as Dhiṣṇis.

## \|\| 1.12.19 \|\|

*teṣāṃ viharaṇīyā ye upastheyāśca ye 'gnayaḥ \|*  
*tāñśṛṇudhvaṃ samāsena kīrtyamānānyathātatham \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. Some of these fires are Viharaṇīyas, (portable, those that should be carried or removed), and others are Upastheyas (those that should be made to sit, deposited (?). They shall be briefly but factually recounted.

## \|\| 1.12.20 \|\|

*vibhuḥ pravāhaṇo gnīdhrastatrasthā dhiṣṇayo 'pare \|*  
*vidhīyante yathāsthānaṃ sūtyāhe savane kramāt \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The following are the sons of Śaṃsya. All of them are remembered by Brāhmaṇas as Upastheyas. Vibhu, Pravahaṇa and Āgnīdhra and others, Dhiṣṇis (already deposited fires) are serially laid down in their proper places in a Savana (Soma sacrifice) on the day when the Soma-juice is extracted.

## \|\| 1.12.21-22 \|\|

*anuddeśya nivāsyānāmagnīnāṃ śṛṇuta kramam \|*  
*samrāḍagni kṛśānuryo dvitīyoṃ'taravedikaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*samrāḍagnamukhānaṣṭau upatiṣṭhanti tān dvijān \|*  
*pariṣatpavamānastu dvitīya so 'nudiśyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Listen to the due order of the fires that are to be laid down Anuddeśya (without being given any particular direction). Brāhmaṇas worship the eight fires beginning with Samrāḍagni. They are Samrāḍagni etc. The second one is Kṛśānu and it is inside the Altar. The third one is Pariṣatpavamāna. It is laid down as directed (anudiśyate).

## \|\| 1.12.23 \|\|

*pratalkānyo nabhonāma catvaresau vibhāvyate \|*  
*havyastato hyasaṃmṛṣṭaḥ śāmitre 'gnau vibhāvyate \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Another fire is Pratalka, (otherwise) named Nabhas. It is manifested in the Catvara (levelled spot of ground specially prepared for the sacrifice), Havya that is not besmeared (with ghee) is deposited in the fire in the Śāmitra vessel (particular vessel used in the sacrifice).

## \|\| 1.12.24 \|\|

*ṛtudhāmā ca sujyotirauduṃbaryaḥ prakīrtyate \|*  
*viśvavyacāḥ samudro 'gnirbrahmasthāne sa kīrtyate \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. (Thereafter is the fire) Ṛtudhāman that is glorified as Sujyoti and Audumbarya Viśvavyacas is the ocean fire? and is glorified in the abode of Brahmā.

## \|\| 1.12.25-26 \|\|

*brahmajyotirvasurdhāmā brahmasthāne sa ucyate \|*  
*acaukapādupastho yaḥ sa vai śālāsukhīyakaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*anuheśyo hyahirbudhnyo so 'grirgṛhapatiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*śaṃsyasyaite sutāḥ sarve upastheyā dvijaiḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. (The fire) Vasurdhāman that is Brahmajyoti is mentioned in the abode of Brahmā. Ajaikapāt that is an Upastheya is also Śālāsukhīyaka. Ahirbudhnya is an Anuddeśya fire. That fire is remembered as Gṛhapati.

## \|\| 1.12.27-28 \|\|

*tato viharaṇīyāṃśca vakṣyāmyaṣṭau ca tatsutān \|*  
*vibhuḥ pravāhaṇo 'gnīdhrasteṣāṃ dhiṣṇyastathā pare \|\| 27 \|\|*

*vidhīyante yathāsthānaṃ sautye 'hni savane kramāt \|*  
*hotrīyastu smṛte hyagnirvahniryo havyavāhanaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Thereafter, I shall enumerate his eight sons who are called Viharaṇīyas. \[Here there is a repetition of verse No. 20\]. The fire Havyavāhana is declared as Hotrīya fire (i.e. fire used by the Hotṛ).

## \|\| 1.12.29-30 \|\|

*praśānto 'gniḥ pracetāstu dvitīyaścātra nāmakaḥ \|*  
*tato 'gnirvaiśvadevastu brāhmaṇācchaṃsirucyate \|\| 29 \|\|*

*uśigagniḥ kaviryastu poto 'gniḥ sa vibhāvyate \|*  
*āvāriragnirvābhārirvaiṣṭhīyaḥ sa vibhāvyate \|\| 30 \|\|*

29-30. The second fire here is named Pracetas that is a subdued fire. Thereafter is the fire Vaiśvadeva. It is called śaṃsi by the Brāhmaṇas. The fire Uśik that is Kavi is conceived as Pota fire. It is also conceived as Āvāri fire, Vābhāri and Vaiṣṭhīya.

## \|\| 1.12.31 \|\|

*avasphūrjo vivasvāṃstu āsthāṃścaiva sa ucyate \|*  
*aṣṭamaḥ sudhyuragniryomārjālīyaḥ sa ucyante \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. The fire Avasphūrja is also called Vivasvān and Āsthān. The eighth one which is fire Sudhyu is also called Mārjālīya.

## \|\| 1.12.32 \|\|

*dhiṣṇyāvāharaṇā hyete sautyehnījyanta vai dvijaiḥ \|*  
*apāṃ yoniḥ smṛto 'sau sa hyapsunāmā vibhāvyate \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Those Dhiṣṇyas, the Viharaṇīyas, are being worshipped on the Sautya day (that is the day on which Soma juice is extracted) by the Brāhmaṇas. It (i.e. Sudhyu) is remembered as the source of origin of the waters. Indeed it is conceived in waters.

## \|\| 1.12.33 \|\|

*tato yaḥ pāvako nāmnā abjo yo garbha ucyate \|*  
*agniḥ so 'vabhṛthe jñeyo varuṇena sahejyate \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. The fire by name Pāvaka that is born of waters and that is called Abgarbha (Having the waters as the womb) should be known as the fire at the Avabhṛtha (the holy ablution at the end of a sacrifice). It is worshipped along with Varuṇa.

## \|\| 1.12.34 \|\|

*tdṛcchayastatsuto hyagnirjaṭhare yo nṛṇāṃ pacan \|*  
*mṛtyumāñ jāṭharasyāgnervidvānāgniḥ sutaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Hṛcchaya (Abiding within the heart) is the fire that is his (Pāvaka’s) son. It is the fire that digests (food-stuffs) in the stomach of men. Mṛtyumān is remembered as the scholarly son of the Jaṭhara-fire (Gastric fire).

## \|\| 1.12.35-36 \|\|

*parasparotthitaḥ so 'gnirbhūtānīha vinirdahet \|*  
*putrastvagnermanyumato ghoraḥ saṃvartakaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*pibannavaḥ sa vasati samudre vaḍavāmukhaḥ \|*  
*samudravāsinaḥ putraḥ sāharakṣo vibhāvyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. That fire born mutually may burn all the living beings here. The terrible Saṃvartaka fire is remembered as the son of the fire Manyumān (? Mṛtyumān). It drinks water and lives in the ocean and has the face of a mare. Saharakṣa is conceived as the son of Samudravāsin (residing within the ocean).

## \|\| 1.12.37 \|\|

*saharakṣasutaḥ kṣāmo gṛhāṇāṃ dahate nṛṇām \|*  
*kravyādagniḥ sutastasya puruṣānatti yo mṛtān \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. Kṣāma, the son of Saharakṣa, burns the houses of men. His son is the fire Kravyād and it consumes dead persons.

## \|\| 1.12.38 \|\|

*ityete pāvakasyāgneḥ putrā eva prakīrttitāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ śucistu vai sauro gandharvairāyurāhutaḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. Thus the sons of Pāvaka fire have been described here. Thereafter is the solar fire Śuci. It is called Āyus by the Gandharvas.

## \|\| 1.12.39 \|\|

*mathito yastvaraṇyāṃ ca so 'gniragniṃ samindhati \|*  
*āyurnāmnā tu bhagavānasau yastu praṇīyate \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. This fire generates other fires on being churned in the Araṇi; this fire is taken from one place to another; this lord is known by the name Āyus.

## \|\| 1.12.40 \|\|

*āyuṣo mahiṣaḥ putraḥ sahaso nāma tatsutaḥ \|*  
*pākayajñeṣvabhīmānī sognistu sahasaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. Mahiṣa was the son of Āyus. His son is named Sahasa. That fire Sahasa is remembered as the Abhimānin (Identifying itself with it) in the Yajñas of Pāka (cooking).

## \|\| 1.12.41 \|\|

*putraśca sahasasyāgneradbhutaḥ sa mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*vividhiścādbhutasyāpi putro 'gnestumāhānsmṛtaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. The son of the fire Sahasa was Adbhuta of great fame. Vividhi is remembered as the great son of the fire Adbhuta.

## \|\| 1.12.42 \|\|

*prāyaścitteṣvabhīmānī hutaṃ bhuṅkte haviḥ sadā \|*  
*vividhestu suto hyarkka stasya cāgneḥ sutā ime \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. (This fire) is one that identifies itself with expiatory rites. It always consumes the Havis-offering that is consigned into the fire. Arkka was the son of Vividhi. The following were the sons of that fire (Arkka).

## \|\| 1.12.43 \|\|

*anīkavān vājasṛk ca rakṣohā caṣṭikṛttathā \|*  
*surabhirvasurannādo praviṣṭo yaḥ sa rukamarāṭ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. They are—Anīkavān, Vājasṛk, Rakṣohā, Yaṣṭikṛt. Surabhi, Vasu, Annāda, Apraviṣṭa and Rukmarāṭ.

## \|\| 1.12.44 \|\|

*śuceragneḥ prajā hyeṣā vahnayaśca caturddaśa \|*  
*ityete cāgnayaḥ proktāḥ praṇīyantedhvareṣu vai \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. These fourteen fires are the Progeny of the fire Śuci. These fires are said to be those that are consecrated in the sacrifices.

## \|\| 1.12.45 \|\|

*ādisarge vyatītā vai yāmaiḥ saha surottamaiḥ \|*  
*svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare pūrvamagnayastebhimāninaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. In the Manvantara of Svāyambhuva in the first Sarga (creation), these fires that are Abhimānins (those that identify themselves) had passed away along with the Yāmas, the excellent Devas.

## \|\| 1.12.46 \|\|

*ete viharaṇīyeṣu cetanācetaneṣu vai \|*  
*sthānābhimānino loke prāgāsanhavyavāhanāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. Formerly in the world, these Havyavāhanas (fires) were those that identified themselves with the abodes called Viharaṇīyas, both sentient and insentient.

## \|\| 1.12.47 \|\|

*kāmyanai mittikā yajñeṣvete karmasvavasthitāḥ \|*  
*pūrvamanvataṃre 'tītāḥ śukairyāgaiśca taiḥ saha \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. These fires were stationed in the holy rites and Yajñas. They were (both) Kāmyas (those with the fruit desired) and Naimittikas occasional ones or that are utilised when cause arises). They had passed away in the previous Manvantara along with those Śukras and Yāgas (?)

## \|\| 1.12.48 \|\|

*devairmahātmabhiḥ puṇyaiḥ prathamasyāntare manoḥ \|*  
*ityetāni majoktāni sthānāni sthāninaśca ha \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. In the Manvantara of the first Manu, they had passed away along with the holy noble-souled Devas. Thus the abodes of these Sthānins (those that identify themselves with the abodes) have been enumerated by me.

## \|\| 1.12.49 \|\|

*taireva tu prasaṃkhyātamatītānāgateṣviha \|*  
*sanvantareṣu sarveṣu lakṣaṇaṃ jātavedasām \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. The characteristics of Jātavedas (fires) in the Manvantaras of the past and future are enumerated through them.

## \|\| 1.12.50 \|\|

*sarve tapasvino hyete sarve brahmabhṛtastathā \|*  
*prajānāṃ patayaḥ sarve jyotiṣmantaśca te smṛtāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. All of them are remembered as ascetics and Brahmabhṛts (those that sustain the knowledge of Brahman). All of them were lords of subjects. They are remembered as Luminous.

## \|\| 1.12.51 \|\|

*svārociṣādiṣu jñeyāḥ sāvarṇyaṃ teṣu saptasu \|*  
*manvantareṣu sarveṣu nāmarūpaprayojanaiḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. These are to be known (as present) in all the seven Manvaṇtaras beginning with Svārociṣa and ending with the Sāvarṇya Manvantara in regard to their names, forms and purposes.

## \|\| 1.12.52 \|\|

*varttante varttamānaiśca yāmaidevaiḥ sahāgnayaḥ \|*  
*anāgataiḥ suraiḥ sārddhaṃ vartsyante 'nāgatāgnayaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The present fires exist along with the current Yāma Devas. The future fires (lit. those that have not yet come) shall exist along with the future Devas.

## \|\| 1.12.53 \|\|

*ityeṣa nicayo 'gnīnāmanukrānto yathākramam \|*  
*vistareṇānupurvyā ca pitṝṇāṃ vakṣyate punaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Thus the group of fires has been duly described in the proper order.

Now henceforth the race of the Pitṛs will be narrated in detail and in the due order.

## Chapter 13 - The Real Nature of Kāla (time)

## \|\| 1.13.1 \|\|

*suta uvāca*  
*brahmaṇaḥ sṛjataḥ putrān pūrvaṃ svāyaṃbhuveṃ'tare \|*  
*gātrebhyo jajñire tasya manuṣyāsuradevatāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

Sūta said:

1\. Even as Brahmā was creating sons formerly in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara, the human beings, the Asuras and the Devas were born out of his limbs.

## \|\| 1.13.2 \|\|

*pitṛvanmanyamānāstaṃ jajñire pitaro 'pi ca \|*  
*teṣāṃ nisargaḥ prāguktaḥ samāsācchruyatāṃ punaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The Pitṛs also were born, considering him as their father (?). The mode of their creation has been described before. Let it be heard briefly once again.

## \|\| 1.13.3 \|\|

*devāsuramanuṣyāṃśca sṛṣṭvā brahmābhyamanyata \|*  
*pitṛvanmanyamānā vai jajñire 'syopapakṣataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. After creating the Devas, Asuras and the human beings, Brahmā took pride in them. (He conceived of a further creation also). (The Pitṛs) who were being considered like fathers, were born of his flanks.

## \|\| 1.13.4 \|\|

*madhvādayaḥ ṣaḍṛtavaḥ pitṝṃstānparicakṣate \|*  
*ṛtavaḥ pitaro devā ityeṣā vaidikī śrutiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The six seasons beginning with Madhu (Spring) (were born of his flanks). They call them Pitṛs. The vedic text says,—“The seasons are the Pitṛs and Devas.”

## \|\| 1.13.5 \|\|

*manvantareṣu sarveṣu hyatītānāgateṣu vai \|*  
*ete svāyaṃbhuve pūrvamutpannāścāntare śubhe \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. In all the Manvantaras, past and future (the same is repeated). Formerly, these were born in the auspicious Manvantara of Svāyambhuva.

## \|\| 1.13.6-9 \|\|

*agniṣvāttā smṛtā nāmnā tathā barhiṣadaśca vai \|*  
*ayajvānastathā teṣāmāsanye gṛhamedhinaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*agniṣvāttā smṛtāste vai pitaro nāhitāgnayaḥ \|*
