12\. Viśāla, the son who was born to him became a king extremely virtuous, liberal in gifts and well renowned for heroism and great power. The city of Viśālā (Vaiśālī) was built by him.

## \|\| 2.61.13 \|\|

*viśālasya suto rājā hemacandro mahābalaḥ \|*  
*sucandra iti vikhyāto hemacandrādanantaraḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. The son of Viśāla was Hemacandra, a king of great strength. The successor of Hemacandra became famous by the name Sucandra.

## \|\| 2.61.14 \|\|

*sucandratanayo rājā dhūmrāśva iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*dhūmrāśvatanayo vidvānsṛṃjayaḥ samapadyata \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Sucandra’s son was a renowned king named Dhūmrāśva. The learned Sṛñjaya was bora as the son of Dhūmrāśva.

## \|\| 2.61.15 \|\|

*sṛñjayasya sutaḥ śrīmānsahadevaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*kṛśāśvaḥ sahadevasya putraḥ paramadhārmikaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The glorious Sahadeva of great exploits was the son of Sṛñjaya. Kṛśāśva, the son of Sahadeva, was extremely righteous.

## \|\| 2.61.16 \|\|

*kṛśāśvasya mahātejā somadattaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*somadattasya rājarṣeḥ suto 'bhūjjanamejayaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. The son of Kṛśāśva, viz. Somadatta was excessively brilliant and valorous. The son of the saintly king Somadatta was Janamejaya.

## \|\| 2.61.17-20 \|\|

*janamejayātmajaścaiva pramatirnāma viśrutaḥ \|*  
*tṛṇabinduprabhāveṇa sarve vaiśālakā nṛpāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dīrghāyuṣo mahātmāno vīryavantaḥ sudhārmikāḥ \|*  
*śaryātermithunaṃ tvāsīdānartto nāma viśrutaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*putraḥ sukanyā kanyā ca bhāryā yā cyavanasya ca \|*  
*ānarttasya tu dāyādo revo nāma suvīryavān \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ānarttaviṣayo yasya purī cāpi kuśasthalī \|*  
*revasya raivataḥ putraḥ kakudmī nāma dhārmikaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

17-20. Janamejaya’s son named Pramati was well-renowned. On account of potentiality of Tṛṇabindu all the Vaiśālaka kings with Viśālā as their capital were long-lived, noble-souled, heroic and very virtuous. Śaryāti begot twins. The son was well-renowned by the name of Ānarta. His daughter was Sukanyā who became the wife of Cyavana. Ānarta’s heir named Reva was very powerful. His realm was called Ānarta and the capital city was Kuśasthalī (later Dvārakā).

Raivata was the son of Reva. Another name of his was Kakudmin. He was virtuous.

## \|\| 2.61.21-22 \|\|

*jyeṣṭho bhrātṛśatasyāsīdrājyaṃ prāpya kuśasthalīm \|*  
*kanyayā saha śrutvā ca gāndharvaṃ brahmaṇoṃ'tike \|\| 21 \|\|*

*muharttaṃ devadevasya mārtyaṃ bahuyugaṃ vibho \|*  
*ājagāma yuvā caiva svāṃ purīṃ yādavairvṛtām \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. He was the eldest of a hundred brothers. After obtaining the kingdom and the capital Kuśasthalī, he went near Brahmā accompanied by his daughter. In the presence of Brahmā, he listened to Gāndharva Music for a short while (A Muhūrta i.e. 48 minutes) as reckoned by the lord of the Devas, but many Yugas according to human calculation. He returned to his city still a young man. The city then was inhabited by the Yādavas.

## \|\| 2.61.23 \|\|

*kṛtāṃ dvāravatīṃ nāma bahudvārāṃ manoramām \|*  
*bhojavṛṣṇyandhakairguptāṃ vasudevapurogamaiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. It had been renamed Dvārāvatī. It was protected by the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, the chief of whom was Vasudeva.

## \|\| 2.61.24 \|\|

*tāṃ kathāṃ revataḥ śrutvā yathātattvamarindamaḥ \|*  
*kanyāṃ tu baladevāya suvratāṃ nāma revatīm \|*  
*dattvā jagāma śikharaṃ merostapasi saṃsthitaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. On hearing the story with all facts, Revata (Raivata) the suppressor of foes gave his daughter of good holy rites named Revatī to Baladeva in marriage. Thereafter, he went to the peak of Meru and became engaged in penance.

## \|\| 2.61.25 \|\|

*reme rāmaśca dharmātmā revatyā sahitaḥ kila \|*  
*tāṃ kathāmṛṣayaḥ śrutvā papracchuktadanantaram \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. Rāma, the noble one, sported with Revatī.

On hearing that story the sages asked him subsequently.

The sages asked:

## \|\| 2.61.26-28 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathaṃ bahuyuge kāle samatīte mahāmate \|*  
*na jarā revatīṃ prāptā raivataṃ vā kakudminam \|*  
*etacchuśrūṣamāṇānno gāndharvaṃ vada caiva hi \|\| 26 \|\|*

*sūta uvāca*  
*na jarā kṣutpipāse vā na ca mṛtyubhayaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*na ca rogaḥ prabhavati brahmalokaṃ gatasya ha \|\| 27 \|\|*

*gāndharvaṃ prati yaccāpi pṛṣṭastu munisattamāḥ \|*  
*tato 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yāthātathyena suvratāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. How was it that old age did not affect Revatī or Kakudmin, O highly intelligent one, even after the lapse of a long time viz. many Yugas?

We are desirous of listening to this. Tell us Gāndharva (the science of Music) too.

## \|\| 2.61.29 \|\|

*sapta svarāstrayo grāmā mūrchanāstvekaviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*tānāścaikonapañcāśadityetsvaramaṇḍalam \|\| 29 \|\|*

Sūta said:

To a person who goes to the world of Brahmā there is neither old age nor hunger nor thirst not even the fear from death. No ailments afflict him. Since I have been asked about Gāndharva (the science of Music). O great and excellent sages of good holy rites, I shall explain it accurately in details.

29\. The Svara-maṇḍala (the whole group in regard to notes) consists of seven notes (Svaras), three Grāmas (Basic scales), twenty-one Mūrcchanās and forty-nine Tānas.

\[see notes on Grāmas, Mūrcchanās and Tānas\]

## \|\| 2.61.30 \|\|

*ṣaḍjaṣabhau ca gāndhāro madhyamaḥ pañcamastathā \|*  
*dhaivataścāpi vijñeyastathā cāpi niṣādakaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. \[The names of the notes:\] Ṣaḍja (Sā), Ṛṣabha (Ri), Gāndhāra (Ga), Madhyama (Ma), Pañcama (Pa), Dhaivata (Dha) and also Niṣāda (Ni) should be (carefully) known (as the notes).

## \|\| 2.61.31-32 \|\|

*sauvīrā madhyamā grāmā hariṇāśca tathaiva ca \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasyāḥ kāloyanopetāścaturthāśuddhamadhyamāḥ \|*  
*nagniṃ ca pauṣā vai deva dṛṣṭvā kāñca yathākramaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. (and part of 33): \[The Text is corrupt and obscure. As emended from Vā P. and other Purāṇas, it gives the names of Mūrchhanās of the Ma-scale as follow\]

The Mūrcchanās of the Ma-scale are known as Sauvīrā, Madhyama-grāmā, Hariṇāsyā (Hariṇāśca in Bd. P. is wrong), Kālopabalopetā (also known as ‘Kālopanatā’), Śuddhamadhyamā, Śārṅgī and Pāvanī (nagniṃ ca pauṣā vai in the text is not correct) and Hṛtyakā Dṛṣṭvā kām’ in the text), in order.

## \|\| 2.61.33-34 \|\|

*madhyamagrāmikākhyātā ṣaḍjagrāmā nibodhata \|*  
*uttaraṃ mandrā rajanī tathā vāconnarāyatāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*madhyaṣaḍjā tathā caiva tathānyā cābhimudgaṇā \|*  
*gāndhāragrāmikā śyāmā kīrtimānā nibodhata \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34a. Now understand the Mūrcchanās of Sa-Scale (Ṣaḍja-grāma): (1) Uttara—mandrā, (2) Rajanī and also as (3) Uttarāyatā (for Unnarāyatā of Bd. P.), (4) Madhya-Ṣaḍja (but Vā. P. Śuddha Ṣaḍja) and also the other one is (5) Abhirudgatā (for Abhi-mudgaṇā in the Bd. P.)

34b. Know the Mūrcchanās of the Ga-scale (Gāndhāra-grāma) viz. Śyāmā as are described.

## \|\| 2.61.35-37 \|\|

*agniṣṭomaṃ tu mādyaṃ tu dvitīyaṃ vājapeyikam \|*  
*yavarātasūyastu ṣaṣṭhavattu suvarmakam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*sapta gausavanā nāma mahāvṛṣṭikatāṣṭamām \|*  
*brahmadānaṃ ca navamaṃ prājāpatyamanantaram \|*  
*nāgayakṣāśrayaṃ vidvān tadgottaratathaiva ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*padakrāntamṛgakrāntaṃ viṣṇukrāntamanoharā \|*  
*sūryakāntadhareṇyaiva saṃtakokilaviśrutaḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. (The names of the Tānas are as follows:)

(1) Agniṣṭomika, (2) Vājapeyika, \[Vā. P. adds (3)Pauṇḍraka, (4) Aśvamedhika\], (5) Rājasūyaka (conjectural emendation for ‘yava-rātasūyastu’ in the text). The sixth is ‘Suvarṇaka,’ the Seventh is ‘Gosava’, the eighth is Mahāvṛṣṭika, the ninth is ‘Brahmadāna,’ the next (10) is Prājāpatya, (11) Nāgayakṣāśraya, (12) Gottara, (13) Paḍakrānta (Vā. P. ‘Haya-Krānta’), (14) Mṛgakrānta, (15) the charming Viṣṇukrānta, (16) the most desirable (vareṇya) Sūryakānta (Vā. P. reading for the obscure Sūryakānta-dhareṇya in Bd. P. is accepted), (17) the well-known Mattakokila (Matta-kokila) of Vā. P. is accepted for Santakokila in the text).

## \|\| 2.61.38 \|\|

*tenavānityapavaśapiśācātīvanahyapi \|*  
*sāvitramardhasāvitraṃ sarvatobhadrameva ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

38a. Obscure and untraced inVā P. and elsewhere.

38b. (The names of Tānas continued:) (18) Sāvitra, (19) Ardha-sāvitra (20) Sarvatobhadra \[After 38-b. here—of Vā. P. adds the following Tānas: Suvarṇa, Sutandra, Viṣṇu, Vaiṣṇuvara, Sāgara and Vijaya which is charming to all\].

## \|\| 2.61.39 \|\|

*manoharamadhātryaṃ ca gandharvānupataśca yaḥ \|*  
*alaṃbuṣeseṣṭamatho viṣṇuvaiṇavarāvubhau \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. (21) The charming Adhātrya, (22) Gandharvānupata (23) Alambuṣeṣṭa, (24) Viṣṇu (25) Vaiṇavara.

## \|\| 2.61.40 \|\|

*sāgarāvijayaṃ caiva sarvabhūtamanoharaḥ \|*  
*hatotsṛṣṭo vijānīta skandhaṃ tu priyameva ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

40a. (26) ‘Sāgaravijaya’ which is charming to all beings (Vā. P. gives ‘Sāgara’ and ‘Vijaya’).

40b. (27) Hatosṛṣṭa and (28) know the likable ‘Skandha’

## \|\| 2.61.41 \|\|

*manoharamadhātryaṃ ca gandharvānupataśca yaḥ \|*  
*alaṃbuseṣṭasya tathā nāradapriya eva ca \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. (Repeats mostly the above verse 39 and adds) Alambuṣeṣṭa and also (29) Nārada-priya.

## \|\| 2.61.42 \|\|

*kathito bhīmasenena nagarātānayapriyaḥ \|*  
*vikalopanītavinatāśrīrākhyo bhārgavapriyaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

42a. As recounted by Bhīmasena (30) Nāgarapriya (dear to citizens), (nāgarāṇāṃ yathā priyaḥ in Vā. P. It is more clear than the obscure ‘nāgaratānayapriyaḥ’ in the text).

42b. (The Tāna) called (31) Vikalopanīta-vinatā Śrīḥ (32) Bhārgavapriya.

## \|\| 2.61.43 \|\|

*caturdaśa tathā pañcadaśecchantīha nāradaḥ \|*  
*sasauvīrāṃ susovīrā brahmaṇo hyapagīyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

43a. The fourteen; similarly they desire here fifteen (according to) Nārada.

43b. (Obscure but from Vā. P. it appears that the presiding deities of the Mūrcchanās are now enumerated. The Bd. P. text may tentatively be interpreted—on the basis of Vā. P. as follows)

(Mūrchanā Gāndhārī) along with Sauvīrā is hence sung by god Brahmā.

## \|\| 2.61.44 \|\|

*uttarādisvaraścaiva brahmā vai devatāstrayaḥ \|*  
*harideśasamutpannā hariṇasyāvyajāyata \|\| 44 \|\|*

44a. And also of the Uttarādi-Svara, god Brahmā is the presiding deity here. \[devatāstrayaḥ’ of the Bd. P. is probably ‘devatātra ca’, as in Vā. P.\]

44b. Hariṇāsyā is originated in the region of Hari.

## \|\| 2.61.45 \|\|

*mūrchanā hariṇā te vai candrasyāsyādhidaivatam \|*  
*karopanītā vivṛtāvanudriḥ svaramaṇḍale \|\| 45 \|\|*

45a. The Mūrcchanā Hariṇāsyā has the Moon-god as the presiding deity (but Indra as per Vā. P.)

45b. The Mūrcchanā Karopanītavitatā is sung by Maruts in the svara-maṇḍala (group of notes).

## \|\| 2.61.46 \|\|

*sākalopanatātasmānmanutasyānnadaivataḥ \|*  
*manudeśāḥ samutpannā mūrcchanāśuddhamātmanā \|\| 46 \|\|*

46a. That is Kalopanītā and hence its presiding Deity is Māruta emended as: Mārutaścātra daivatam, as in Vā. P.).

46b. Śuddha-madhyamā (emended as per Vā. P. for Śuddha-mātmanā) mūrcchanā is originated in Manu (Maru) deśa (After 46 b Vā. P. adds:)

Śuddha Madhyamā is the note here and the deity is Gandharva. It moves along with the deer for the guidance of Siddhas.

## \|\| 2.61.47 \|\|

*tasmāttasmānmṛgāmargīmṛgendrosyādhidaivatā \|*  
*sāvaśramasamādyumnā anekāpauruṣānakhān \|\| 47 \|\|*

47a. Hence, on account of Mṛgas (deer) it (the Mūrcchanā is called Mārgī and the Lion is its deity.

47b: Obscure:

(Tentative meaning: ‘That is associated with hermitages and various human voices’ (?)\]

## \|\| 2.61.48 \|\|

*mūrcchanāyojanāhyeṣāsyādrajasārajanītataḥ \|*  
*tāni uttara madrāṃsapadgadaivatakaṃ viduḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48a. As the Mūrcchanā is associated with rajas (atmosphere/mist), it is called Rajanī.

48b. Obscure (If allied with Vā. P.:)

Uttaramandrā is known as having Ṣaḍja as its deity.

## \|\| 2.61.49 \|\|

*tasmāduttaratāyāvatprathamaṃ svāyamaṃ viduḥ \|*  
*tamoduttaramaidroyadevatāsyādruvena ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

49\. Obscure (If allied with Vā. P.):

Hence Uttara-tāla is known first as well extended.

Hence, it is Uttara-mandrā whose deity indeed is Dhruva.

## \|\| 2.61.50 \|\|

*apāmaduttaratvāvadhaivatasyottarāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*syādijamūrchanāhyeca pitaraḥ śrāddhadevatāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

50\. Obscure (emended from Vā. P.)

Because of its extension and being later (in the order) Uttarāyatā having Dha (Dhaivata) as the starting point, is the Mūrcchanā, the deity of which is the manes, the deities of Śrāddha.

## \|\| 2.61.51 \|\|

*śuddhaṣaḍjasvara kṛtvā yasmādagnimaharṣayaḥ \|*  
*upaiti tasmānnajānī yācchuddhayacchikarāsabhā \|\| 51 \|\|*

51a. The great sages worship the Fire-god with the Śuddha Ṣaḍja (Pure Sa-) note. Hence, one should know it as Śuddha-Ṣaḍjikā (Vā. P.: This Mūrcchanā starts from the Pañcama note).

51b. is obscure, hence the reading in Vā. P. is followed.

## \|\| 2.61.52 \|\|

*ityetā mūrchanāḥ kṛtvā yasyāmīdṛśabhāvanaḥ \|*  
*pakṣiṇāṃ mūrchanāḥ śrutvā pakṣokā mūrchanāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52a. In this manner employing these Mūrcchanās in which he has got such Bhāvanā (particular faith).

52b. The mūrcchanās belong to Yakṣīs (female Yakṣas) are called Yakṣikā mūrcchanās (Ya in the Ms seems to have been read as Pa, as in writing in Devanāgarī script Pa & Ya look similar).

## \|\| 2.61.53 \|\|

*nāgādṛṣṭiviṣāgītānopasarpantimūrchanāḥ \|*  
*nānāsādhāramaścaivavaḍavātrividastathā \|\| 53 \|\|*

53a (Obscure but if allied with Vā. P.)

The Mūrcchanās do not approach the songs, affected by the poisonous sight of the serpents (Nāgas).

53b (Corrupt and obscure but with the help of Vā. P.)

And there are many Sādhāraṇa mūrcchanās (and also six only (?) are known thoroughly, (The reading Vaḍavātrividastathā in the text is obscure. Vā. P. gives Ṣaḍevānuvidastathā).

## Chapter 62 - The science of music

## \|\| 2.62.1 \|\|

*pūrvācāryamataṃ buddhvā pravakṣyāmyanupūrvaśaḥ \|*  
*vikhyātānvai alaṅkārāṃstanme nigadataḥ śruṇu \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. After knowing the views of earlier teachers, I shall expound the well-known embellishments in music in due order. Please listen to them, while I am explaining.

## \|\| 2.62.2 \|\|

*alaṅkārāstu vaktavyāḥ svaiḥ svairvarṇaiḥ prahetavaḥ \|*  
*saṃsthā nayogaiśca tathā sadā nāḍhyādyavekṣayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The embellishments are to be spoken of along with their Varṇas (movements of notes such as ‘steady’, ‘ascending and others) as their specific basis and also along with their associated configuration (saṃsthāna), always in regard to dramatic performance etc.

## \|\| 2.62.3 \|\|

*vākyārthapadayogārthairalaṅkāraiśca pūraṇam \|*  
*padāni gītakasyāhuḥ purastātpṛṣṭhato 'tha vā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3a. The fulfilment of embellishment is achieved by the implications of sentences and connotations of the word-combinations.

3b. The words of the song are said to be either preceding or following the embellishment.

## \|\| 2.62.4 \|\|

*sthātonitrīnaro nīḍḍīmanaḥkaṇṭhaśirasthayā \|*  
*eteṣu triṣu sthāneṣu pravṛtto vidhiruttamaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

4a: (Bd. P. text corrupt & obscure but Vā. P. reads) One should know that the following three are the places of Utterances viz. the chest, throat and head.

4b. In these three places, the best procedure (of producing notes) functions.

## \|\| 2.62.5 \|\|

*cattvāraḥ prakṛtau varṇāḥ pravicārasya nurvidhā \|*  
*vikalpamaṣṭadhā caiva devāḥ ṣoḍaśadhā viduḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5a. In the original stage (Prakṛtau), there are four Varṇas (tone-patterns) having fourfold movements.

5b. The alternative movements are eightfold; and gods know them as sixteenfold.

## \|\| 2.62.6 \|\|

*sṛṣṭo varmaḥ prasaṃcārī tṛtīyamavarohaṇam \|*  
*ārohaṇaṃ caturthaṃ tu varṇaṃ varmavido viduḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. (The names of Varṇas:)

The first Varṇa is Sthāyin, the second is Prasañcārin, the third is Avarohaṇa (= Avarohin) and the fourth Varṇa is known by the experts in the knowledge of Varṇas to be Ārohaṇa (= Ārohin).

## \|\| 2.62.7 \|\|

*tatraikaḥ saṃcarasthāyī saṃcarastu caro 'bhavat \|*  
*avarohaṇavarṇānāmavarohaṃ vinirdiśet \|\| 7 \|\|*

7a. There is one (Varṇa i.e. Sthāyin) which has steady employment. The Sañcāra is the mixed movement.

7b. One should indicate the descent of Varṇas (i.e. Svaras) as Avarohaṇa.

## \|\| 2.62.8 \|\|

*ārohaṇena vārohānvarṇānvarṇavido viduḥ \|*  
*eteṣāmeva varṇānāmalaṅkārannibodhata \|\| 8 \|\|*

8a. (Vā. P.) And the experts in the knowledge of Varṇas know (that varṇa) as the Āroha-Varṇa by the ascent of notes.

8b. Now know then the embellishments of these specific Varṇas.

## \|\| 2.62.9 \|\|

*alaṅkārāstu catvārasthāpanī kramarejanaḥ \|*  
*pramādasyāpramādaśca teṣāṃ vakṣyāmi lakṣaṇam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. There are four embellishments viz. Sthāpanī, Kramarejana, Pramāda and Apramāda. I shall explain the characteristics of these.

## \|\| 2.62.10 \|\|

*visvaro 'ṣṭakalāścaiva sthānaṃ dvyekatarāgataḥ \|*  
*āvarttasyākramo tvākṣī vekāryāṃ parimāṇataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. (Names of Alaṅkāras continue as follows:) Visvara, Aṣṭakala which has an interval of one place (from its original place?); Āvarta and Kramotpatti—These two should be effected according to their proportion.

## \|\| 2.62.11 \|\|

*kumāraṃ saṃparaṃ viddhi dvistaraṃ vāmanaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*eṣa vai eṣa caivasyakutarekaḥ kulādhikaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11a. One should know the other one to be Kumāra and also Vistara.

11b. And this indeed is fhe Apāṅga (alaṅkāra) and Kutareka (?) possesses one more Kalā (Time-measure)

## \|\| 2.62.12 \|\|

*sveta sve kātare jātakalāmagnitaraiṣitaḥ \|*  
*tasmiṃścaiva svare vṛddhirniṣṭapte tadvicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12a. (Vā. P.) Śyena is originated as having one interval and situated in the midst of Mātrās of a Kalā.660 661 662 663 664

12b. (Vā. P.) In it there abides the increase in the order of the note different from it (e.g. Sā—Pā,—Ri—Dha, Ga—ni).

## \|\| 2.62.13 \|\|

*syenastu aparo hasta uttaraḥ kamalākalaḥ \|*  
*pramāṇaghasabindurnā jāyate vidure punaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13a. (Vā. P.) The descent of the Śyena Alaṅkāra is called Uttara.

13b. (Vā. P.) The Alaṅkāra called Bindu is originated due to the measure of Kalās.

## \|\| 2.62.14 \|\|

*kalā kāryā tu varṇānāṃ tadā nuḥ sthāpito bhavet \|*  
*viparyayasya ropisyā dyasya prādurghaṭī mama \|\| 14 \|\|*

14a. One Kalā (a measure of time) should be employed of the Varṇas. Then it would be Sthāpita (established?).

14b. Durghaṭita is that which has the note even in the reverse order.

## \|\| 2.62.15 \|\|

*ekottaraḥ svarastu syātṣaḍjataḥ paramaḥ svaraḥ \|*  
*akṣepaskandanākāryaṃ kākasyoyacapuṣkalam \|\| 15 \|\|*

15a. Ekottara-Svara has the highest note from Ṣaḍja.

15b. Ākṣepāskandana should be effected as having high amplitude like the (harsh) crowing of the crow.

## \|\| 2.62.16 \|\|

*saṃtārau taunusarvāyyau kāryaṃ vā kāraṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*ākṣiptamavarohyāsītprokṣamadyastathaiva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

16a. The two Santāras belong to Sañcārin Varṇa either as the cause or the effect.

16b. Ākṣipta belongs to the category of the descending (Avarohin) Varṇa.

## \|\| 2.62.17 \|\|

*dvādaśe ca kalāsthānāmekāntaragatas tathā \|*  
*preśollikhitamalaṅkāramevasvarasamanvitā \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. The Alaṅkāra called Preṅkholita has the twelfth place of Kalā having one interval. Thus it is endowed with the notes (?)

## \|\| 2.62.18 \|\|

*svarasvarabahugrāmakāprayoṣṭanupatkalā \|*  
*prakṣiptameva kalayācopādānārayo bhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

18a. (Vā. P.) Puṣkala is said to be due to the transfer of notes.

18b. Prakṣipta is due to Kalā... (?)

## \|\| 2.62.19 \|\|

*dvikathaṃvāvathābhūtayatrabhāṣitamucyate \|*  
*uccarādviśvarārūḍhātathāyāṣṭasvarātathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

19a. It is called Bhāṣita in which there is the use of two Kalās as before.

19b. Visvarārūḍhā (Visarārūḍhā) has got eight notes in ascendance.

## \|\| 2.62.20 \|\|

*vāpaḥ syādavaroheṇa nārato bhavati dhruvam \|*  
*ekāntaraṃ ca hyetevaitamevasvarasattamaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

20a. Vāpa (?) certainly is due to the descent from the high or low register (?).

20b. These are placed verily with one interval and have the same note at the end.

## \|\| 2.62.21 \|\|

*sakṣipracchedanāmācacatuṣkalagaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*alaṅkārā bhavantyete triṃśaddevaiḥ prakīrttitāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Makṣi-praccheda (?) is declared to have a group of four Kalās. Thus, these are the thirty Alaṅkāras explained.

## \|\| 2.62.22 \|\|

*varṇāsthānaprayogeṇa kalāmātrāpramāṇataḥ \|*  
*saṃsthānaṃ ca pramāṇaṃ ca vikāro lakṣaṇastathā \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Due to employment of Varṇa and Sthāna having the measure of Kalā and Mātrā are the configuration, proportion, modification and characteristics.

## \|\| 2.62.23-25 \|\|

*caturvidhamidaṃ jñeya malaṅkāraprayojanam \|*  
*yathātmano hyalaṅkāro vipayasto vigarhitaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*varmamevāpyalaṅkarttuṃ viṣamāhyātmasaṃbhavāḥ \|*  
*nānābharaṇasaṃyogā yathā nāryā vibhūṣaṇam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*varmasya caivālaṅkāro vibhūṣā hyātmasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*na pāde kuṇḍalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ na kaṇṭhe rasanā tathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-24a. This should be known as the purpose of embellishment which is fourfold. Just as in the case of embellishment if it is used at the wrong place it is censured, similarly to beautify even the Varṇas unfavourably, the producer by oneself (?) would be blamed.

24b-25a. Just as due to the use of various ornaments, a woman gets herself beautified, the embellishment is the decoration of Varṇa born of itself (?).

25b. The ear-ring is not seen (worn) on the feet, nor the girdle round the neck.

## \|\| 2.62.26 \|\|

*evamevādyalaṅkāre viparyasto vigarhitaḥ \|*  
*kriyamāṇo 'pyalaṅkāro nāgaṃ yaścaiva darśayat \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thus the embellishment if used in a wrong place is censured. When the embellishment is effected, it should indicate the Rāga (melody).

## \|\| 2.62.27 \|\|

*yathādṛṣṭasya mārgasyakarttavyasyavidhīyate \|*  
*lakṣaṇaṃparyavasyāpivarttikā mapivarttate \|\| 27 \|\|*

27a. Just as the characterisation of the path intended to be undertaken is enjoined by indicating it with a brush.

27b. (?)

## \|\| 2.62.28 \|\|

*yāthātathyena vakṣyāmi māsodbhavamukhodbhava \|*  
*trayoviṃśatiśītistu vijñātapavadaivatam \|\| 28 \|\|*

28a. I shall describe realistically (as it is)....?

28b. Obscure.

## \|\| 2.62.29 \|\|

*nagonātupurastānumadhyamāṃśastu paryayaḥ \|*  
*tayorvibhāgo devānāṃ lāvaṇye mārgasaṃsthitaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29a. Obscure (both in the Bd. P. and Vā. P.)

29b. The division of these two (viz. Ṣaḍja and Madhyama) as the dominant notes brings about the Charm of the songs.

## \|\| 2.62.30 \|\|

*anuṣaṅgamayo dṛṣṭaṃ svasāraṃ vasvarātara \|*  
*viparyayaḥ saṃvartto ca saptasvarapadakramam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30a. Obscure.

30b. (Vā. P.j The reverse would take place in the case of the order of seven notes.

## \|\| 2.62.31-32 \|\|

*gāndhārasetugīyante varomadbhagavānica \|*  
*pañcamaṃmadhyamañcaivadhaivataṃ tu niṣādataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*ṣaḍjarṣabhaścajānīmomadrakeṣvevanāntare \|*  
*dvevdyaparatukiṃvidyāddvayamuṣṇantikasyatu \|\| 32 \|\|*

31a. (Vā. P.) The four Madraka Gītas are sung with Gāndhāra as the keynote.

31b-32a. In Madraka Gītas we know the notes Pañcama (Pa), Madhyama(Ma), Dhaivata (Dha), Niṣāda (Nī), Ṣaḍja (Sā) and Ṛṣabha (Ri) as the remaining notes.

32b. One should know two Aparāntika Songs (?) (The Rest is obscure).

## \|\| 2.62.33 \|\|

*prākṛte vaikṛte caiva gāndhāraḥ sa prayujyate \|*  
*padasyātyayarūpantusaptarūpantukauśikīm \|\| 33 \|\|*

33a. In the Aparāntika songs Gāndhāra (Ga) is employed in the original (Śuddha) form and its modified form.

33b. (Vā. P.) The Pada has got thiee forms (?). The Kaiśikī song has seven forms.

## \|\| 2.62.34 \|\|

*gāndhārasyenakārtsyena cāyaṃ yasyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*eṣacaivakramoddiṣṭomadhyamāṃśasya madhyamaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

34a. With the entire use of Gāndhāra as the keynote procedure of which is declared.

34b. This is also the order intended for its Madhyama as the keynote.

## \|\| 2.62.35 \|\|

*yāni proktāni gītānivaturūpaṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*tataḥ saptasvaraṅkāryaṃsaptarūpañcakauśikī \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. The songs which have been mentioned and particularly those of fourfold form (?) should be effected with seven notes and the Kaiśikī of sevenfold form.

## \|\| 2.62.36 \|\|

*agadarśanamityāhurmānudvaimamaketathā \|*  
*dvitīyāmāsamātrāṇābhiḥ sarvāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36a. This is called as the pointing out of the components (of songs?).

(The Topic of Tāla:) There are two even measures Caturasra (of four beats and eight Mātrās) and Tryasra (four beats and six Mātrās).

36b. Obscure (in Bd. P. & Vā. P.)

## \|\| 2.62.37 \|\|

*uttarevaprakṛtyevaṃmātābrāhmatalāyata \|*  
*tathāhatānopiḍakeyatramāyāṃnivarttate \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. (Vā. P) In Uttara songs in the original form, the Mātrā is thus deleted (the rest is obscure).

## \|\| 2.62.38 \|\|

*pādenaikenamāyātrā pādonāmativārimaḥ \|*  
*saṃkhyāpanopahūtāṃvaitatrapānamiti smṛtam \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. With one foot in the Mātrā and deficiency in one foot... when there is the Upahanana (error?) of numbers in it, it is called Yāna.

## \|\| 2.62.39 \|\|

*dvitīyapādabhaṅgañcagrahenāmapratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*pūrvamaṣṭhatīṭatī nadvitīyaṃ cāparāntikaiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. The second break in the foot is well-established with Graha (the starting point of the song) and in the Aparāntika the first, eighth, third and second are established with Graha?

## \|\| 2.62.40 \|\|

*pādabhāgasapādaṃ tu prakṛtyamapi saṃsthitam \|*  
*caturthamuttaraṃ caivamadravatpāvamadrakau \|\| 40 \|\|*

40\. In the Uttara and in Mandraka songs in their original form, the Pāda-bhāga and also along with one and a quarter (of a Pāda) (?) is in Uttara and Mandraka.

## \|\| 2.62.41 \|\|

*madrakodakṣiṇasyāpi yathoktā varttate kalā \|*  
*sarvamevānuyogaṃ tu dvitīyaṃ buddhimiṣyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41 a. In Mandraka songs the Kalā exists as explained of the Dakṣiṇa mārga also.

41b. Obscure (in both the Purāṇas).

## \|\| 2.62.42-43 \|\|

*pādauvāharaṇaṃ cāsyātpāraṃ nātra vidhīyate \|*  
*ekatvaṃ munuyogasya dvayoryadyaddvijottama \|\| 42 \|\|*

*anekasamavāyastu pātakā hariṇā smṛtāḥ \|*  
*tisṛṇāṃ caiva vṛttīnāṃ vṛttau vṛtte ca dakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42a. Obscure (in both the Purāṇas).

42b-43a. When there is the use of one and the use of two, O best of Brāhmaṇas, and when there is the combination of many, Patākā etc. are declared.

43b. There are three Vṛttis—Citrā, Vṛtti and Dakṣiṇā.

## \|\| 2.62.44 \|\|

*aṣṭau tu samavāyastu vīrā saṃmūrchanā tathā \|*  
*kasyanāsutarācaiva svaraśākhā prakīrttitā \|\| 44 \|\|*

44a. (Vā. P.) The samavāyas (combinations of (?) are eight and similarly, the Mūrcchanā is Sauvīrī.

44b. Obscure: Last foot. Thus the Svara-maṇḍala (the whole group of notes in music) is explained.

## Chapter 63 - The Ikṣvāku dynasty (vaṃśa)

## \|\| 2.63.1 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*kukudminanastu taṃ lokaṃ raivatasya gatasya ha \|*  
*tdṛtā puṇyajanaiḥ sarvā rākṣasaiḥ sākuśasthalī \|\| 1 \|\|*

Note: vide Vā.P. chapter 88.

Sūta said:—

1\. When Raivata, otherwise known as Kakudmin, went to that world (of Brahmā), his city, Kuśasthalī, was completely over-run and captured by Puṇyajanas (Yakṣas) and Rākṣasas.

## \|\| 2.63.2 \|\|

*tadvai bhrātṛśataṃ tasya dhārmikasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*nibadhyamānaṃ nārācairvidiśaḥ prādravadbhayāt \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. The hundred brothers of that virtuous and noble-souled king were afflicted by arrows. Therefore, they fled in every direction due to fear.

## \|\| 2.63.3 \|\|

*teṣāṃ tu tadbhayakrāntakṣatriyāṇāṃ ca vidrutām \|*  
*anvavāyastu sumahāṃstatra tatra dvijottamāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O excellent Brāhmaṇas, the dynasty of these Kṣatriyas who fled due to excessive fright, is very great. They are present in different places.

## \|\| 2.63.4 \|\|

*śāryātā iti vikhyātā dikṣu sarvāsu dharmikāḥ \|*  
*dhṛṣṭasya dharṣṭikaṃ sarvaṃ raṇadhṛṣṭaṃ babhūva ha \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. They are well-known in all the quarters as Śaryātas. They are righteous. The line of Dhṛṣṭa is called Dhārṣṭika. All the members were bold and aggressive in battle.

## \|\| 2.63.5-6 \|\|

*trisāhasraṃ tu sa gaṇaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahātmanām \|*  
*nabhagasya ca dāyādo nābhādo nāma vīryavān \|\| 5 \|\|*

*aṃbarīṣastu nābhāgirvirūpastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*pṛṣadaśvo virūpasya tasya putro rathītaraḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. That clan of those noble-souled Kṣatriyas consisted of three thousand (families). Nabhāga’s heir was the hero named Nābhāga. Ambarīṣa was the son of Nābhāga. His son was Virūpa. Pṛṣadaśva was the son of Virūpa and his son was Rathītara.

## \|\| 2.63.7 \|\|

*ete kṣatraprasūtā vai punaścāṅgirasaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*rathītarāṇāṃ pravarāḥ kṣetropetā dvijātayaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. These were born of Kṣatriyas but are remembered as having become Aṅgiras. The excellent members of Rathītara family were Brāhmaṇas as well as Kṣatriyas.

## \|\| 2.63.8 \|\|

*kṣuvatastu manoḥ pūrvamikṣvākurabhiniḥsṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasya putraśataṃ tvāsīdikṣvākorbhūridakṣimam \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Formerly, when Manu sneezed, Ikṣvāku was born. Ikṣvāku had a hundred sons who distributed much wealth as religious gifts.

## \|\| 2.63.9 \|\|

*teṣāṃ śreṣṭho vikukṣistu nimirdaṇḍaśca te trayaḥ \|*  
*śakunipramukhāstasya putrāḥ pañcāśatastu te \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Vikukṣi, Nimi and Daṇḍa, these three were the most excellent among them. He had fifty sons, the chief of whom was Śakuni.

## \|\| 2.63.10-11 \|\|

*uttarāpathadeśasya rakṣitāro mahīkṣitaḥ \|*  
*catvāriṃśattathāṣṭau ca dakṣiṇasyāṃ tu vai diśi \|\| 10 \|\|*

*virāṭapramukhāste ca dakṣiṇāpatharakṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*ikṣvākustu vikukṣiṃ vai aṣṭakāyāmathā diśat \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. They were the kings protecting Uttarāpatha Northern territory. Forty-eight of them, the father of whom was Virāṭa were the defenders of Dakṣiṇāpatha (Southern territory), in the Southern quarter.

Once, at the performance of the Aṣṭaka (a kind of Śrāddha), Ikṣvāku commanded Vikukṣi thus.

## \|\| 2.63.12 \|\|

*rājovāca \|*  
*māṃsamānaya śrāddhe tvaṃ mṛgānhatvā mahābala \|*  
*śrāddhaṃ mama tu karttavyamaṣṭakānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

The King said:—

12\. “Fetch flesh for the sake of Śrāddha, O highly powerful one, after killing animals. The Śrāddha of Aṣṭaka has to be performed by me surely.”

## \|\| 2.63.13 \|\|

*sa gato mṛgayāṃ caiva vacanāttasya dhīmataḥ \|*  
*mṛgānsahasrakānhatvā pariśrāntaśca vīryavān \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. At the instance of the intelligent one, he went for hunting. After killing thousands of animals, the powerful prince became tired.

## \|\| 2.63.14-15 \|\|

*bhakṣayacchaśakaṃ tatra vikukṣirmṛgayāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*āgate hi vikukṣai tu samāṃse mahasainike \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vasiṣṭhaṃ codayāmāsa māṃsa prokṣayatāmiti \|*  
*tatheti codito rājñā vidhivattadupasthitam \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Vikukṣi who had gone for hunting, ate a rabbit. When Vikukṣi returned with the meat and his army, the king urged Vasiṣṭha saying “Let the meat be sprinkled (with holy water)”. Vasiṣṭha said “So be it”. On being urged thus the meat was duly presented by the king. On seeing the meat polluted, Vasiṣṭha became angry and spoke to him:—

## \|\| 2.63.16-18 \|\|

*sa dṛṣṭvopahataṃ māṃsaṃ kruddho rājānamabravīt \|*  
*anenopahataṃ māṃsaṃ putreṇa tava pārthiva \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śaśabhakṣādaduṣṭaṃ vai naiva māṃsaṃ mahādyute \|*  
*śaśo durātmanā pūrvamamanā bhakṣito 'nagha \|\| 17 \|\|*

*tena māṃsamidaṃ duṣṭaṃ pitṝṇāṃ nṛpasattama \|*  
*ikṣvākustu tataḥ kruddho vikukṣimidamabravīt \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. “This meat has been defiled by your son, O king. By eating the rabbit, O king of great splendour, the meat cannot remain unpolluted. O sinless one, rabbit has been eaten earlier by this wicked fellow. Therefore, O excellent king, this meat intended to be offered to the Pitṛs is defiled”.

Thereupon, Ikṣvāku became furious and spoke this to Vikukṣi:

## \|\| 2.63.19-21 \|\|

*pitṛkarmaṇi nirdiṣṭo mayā ca mṛgayāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*śaśaṃ bhakṣayase 'raṇye nirghṛṇaḥ pūrvamadya tu \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tasmātparityajāmi tvāṃ gaccha tvaṃ svena karmaṇā \|*  
*evamikṣvākuṇā tyakto vasiṣṭhavacanātsutaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ikṣvākausaṃsthite tasmiñchaśādaḥ pṛthivīmimām \|*  
*prāptaḥ paragadharmātmā sa cāyodhyādhipo 'bhavat \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. “Directed by me in connection with the holy rite of the Manes, you went for hunting. But you ate the flesh of the rabbit in the forest earlier to-day. You have been unkind (in this context), Hence, I am banishing you. Go anywhere else along with your own fate”.

Thus he was abandoned by Ikṣvāku. He came to be known by the name Śaśāda (one who eats rabbit). Later, the son became extremely virtuous. When Ikṣvāku passed away he got the entire Earth at the instance of Vasiṣṭha. He became the ruler of Ayodhyā.

## \|\| 2.63.22-23 \|\|

*tadākarotsa rājyaṃ vai vasiṣṭhaparinoditaḥ \|*  
*tatastenainasā pūrṇo rājyāvastho mahīpatiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kālena gatavānso 'tha śakṛnmūtrataraṅgitam \|*  
*jñātvaivametadākhyānaṃ nā vidhirbhakṣayedbudhaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Urged and guided by Vasiṣṭha, he ruled over the kingdom for some time. Even when he was ruling over the kingdom, the king was fully afflicted by this sin. After some time, he fell into the hell, having waves of urine and faeces. After reading this anecdote, a learned man should understand (its implications). He should not eat anything against the Veclic injunction.

## \|\| 2.63.24 \|\|

*māṃsabhakṣayitāmutra yasya māṃsamihādmyaham \|*  
*etanmāṃsasya māṃsatvaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Learned men explain the etymological meaning of Māṃsa (flesh) thus:—

(The being) whose flesh I am eating here shall eat me (Māṃ—me, sa—he bkakṣayitā—shall eat) in the next birth. This is the Māṃsatva (state of being flesh) of meat.

## \|\| 2.63.25-26 \|\|

*śaśādasya tu dāyādaḥ kakutstho nāma vīryavān \|*  
*indrasya vṛṣabhūtasya kakutstho jayate purā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*pūrvamāḍībake yuddhe kakutsthastena saṃsmṛtaḥ \|*  
*anenāstu kakutsthasya pṛthuścānena sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

25-26. Śaśāda’s heir was a heroic king named Kakutstha. Formerly, there was the Āḍibaka fight. In it Indra took the form of a bull. This king seated himself on the hump of the bull (Indra). (Kakut—hump, tstha—occupant) and won the war. Hence, he is remembered as Kakutstha.

Kakutstha’s son was Anenas and Pṛthu was the son of Anenas.

## \|\| 2.63.27-28 \|\|

*dṛṣadaśvaḥ pṛthoḥ putrastasmādandhrastu vīryavān \|*  
*andhrāttu yuvanāśvastu śāvastastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*jajñe śrāvastako rājā śrāvastī yena nirmitā \|*  
*śrāvastasya tu dāyādo bṛhadaśvo mahāyaśāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Dṛṣadaśva was the son of Pṛthu. The powerful (king) Andhra (came) after him. Yuvanāśva was the successor of Andhra. Śrāvasta was born as his son. Śrāvasta became a king by whom the city of Śrāvastī \[Mod. Sahet-Mahet on the Rapti River in Oudh U.P\] was founded. Śrāvasta’s heir was Bṛhadaśva of great renown.

## \|\| 2.63.29 \|\|

*bṛhadaśvasutaścāpi kuvalāśva iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*yastu dhundhuvadhādrājā dhundhumāratvamāgataḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Bṛhadaśva’s son was renowned as Kuvalāśva. This king later on came to be known as Dhundhumāra since he slew the demon Dhundhu.

The sages requested:—

## \|\| 2.63.30 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*dhundhorvadhaṃ mahāprājña ghotumicchāma vistarāt \|*  
*yadarthaṃ kuvalāśvasya dhundhumāratvamāgatam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. We wish to hear in detail, O sage of great intelligence, how Dhundhu was killed, on account of which Kuvalāśva came to be called Dhundhumāra.

Sūta replied:—

## \|\| 2.63.31-33 \|\|

*sūta uvāca*  
*kuvalāśvasya putrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇyekaviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*sarve vidyāsu niṣṇātā balavanto durāsadāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*babhūvurdhārmikāḥ sarve yajvāno bhūridakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*kuvalāśvaṃ mahāvīryaṃ śūramuttamadhārmikam \|\| 32 \|\|*

*bṛhadaśvo hyabhyaṣiñcattasminrājye narādhipaḥ \|*  
*putrasaṃkrāmitaśrīstu vanaṃ rājā viveśa ha \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. Kuvalāśva had twenty-one thousand sons. All of them were experts in different lores. They were strong and unassailable. All of them were righteous. They performed sacrifices and distributed plenty of monetary gifts. Bṛhadaśva the elderly ruler enthroned Kuvalāśva in that realm. Kuvalāśva was very powerful, excellent and virtuous. After transferring the royal position and splendour to his son, the king entered the forest.

## \|\| 2.63.34 \|\|

*bṛhadaśvaṃ mahārājaṃ śūramuttamadhārmikam \|*  
*prayāsyantamutaṅkastu brahmarṣiḥ pratyavārayat \|\| 34 \|\|*

34\. Uttaṅka the Brahminical sage, prevented the great king Bṛhadaśva who was brave, excellent and virtuous, from going to the forest.

## \|\| 2.63.35 \|\|

*uttaṅka uvāca*  
*bhavatā rakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ tattāvatkarttumarhati \|*  
*nirudvignastapaschartuṃ na hi śakro 'pi pārthiva \|\| 35 \|\|*

Uttaṅka said:—

35\. “The duty of protecting people should be carried out by you. It behoves you to do it. O king, I am unable to perform penance unperturbed.

## \|\| 2.63.36 \|\|

*mamāśramasamīpeṣu merorhi paritastu vai \|*  
*samudro vālukāpūrṇastatra tiṣṭhati bhūpate \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. Near the precincts of my hermitage, on the other side of Meru, the ocean is filled with sand, O king.

## \|\| 2.63.37-38 \|\|

*devatānāmavadhyastu mahākāyo mahābalaḥ \|*  
*antarbhūmigatastatra vālukāntarhito mahān \|\| 37 \|\|*

*rākṣasasya madhoḥ putro dhundhurnāma mahāsuraḥ \|*  
*śete lokavināśāya tapa āsthāya dāruṇam \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. A great Asura named Dhundhu is lying underground there hidden by the sands. He cannot be killed by the Devas. He has a huge body and is very powerful. He is the son of Rākṣasa Madhu. After performing terrible penance, he stays there for the destruction of the people.

## \|\| 2.63.39 \|\|

*saṃvatsarasya paryante sa niśvāsaṃ vimuñcati \|*  
*yadā tadā mahī tatra calati sma sakānanā \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. When he exhales at the end of a year, the ground there quakes and shakes along with the forests.

## \|\| 2.63.40-41 \|\|

*tasya niśvāsavātena raja uddhūyate mahat \|*  
*ādityapathamāvṛtya saptāhaṃ bhūmikaṃpanam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*savisphuliṅgaṃ sajvāraṃ sadhūmamatidāruṇam \|*  
*tena rājanna śaknomi tasminsthātuṃ sva āśrame \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. A great column of dust is raised by the air exhaled by him. It envelops the path of the sun. The Earthquake continues for a week. It is extremely terrifying, as it is accompanied by sparks, flames and fumes. Hence, O king, I am unable to stay within my hermitage.

## \|\| 2.63.42 \|\|

*taṃ vāraya mahābāho lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|*  
*tejaste sumahadviṣmustejasāpyāyayiṣyati \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Resist him, O king of great powerful arms, with a desire for the welfare of the worlds. Your brilliant splendour is already great. Viṣṇu will develop it further by contribution of h is own splendour.

## \|\| 2.63.43 \|\|

*lokāḥ svasthā bhavantvadya tasminvinihate sure \|*  
*tvaṃ hi tasya vadhārthāya samarthaḥ pṛthivīpate \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Indeed, you alone are capable of slaying him, O lord of the Earth. Let the worlds become happy and relieved with that Asura slain.

## \|\| 2.63.44-45 \|\|

*viṣṇunā ca varo datto mama pūrva yato 'nagha \|*  
*na hi dhundhurmahāvīryastejasālpena śākyate \|\| 44 \|\|*

*nirdagdhuṃ pṛthivīpālairapi varṣaśatairapi \|*  
*vīryaṃ hi sumahattasya devairapi durāsadam \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. O sinless one, formerly, a boon had been granted to me (that you would help me by killing him). Indeed, Dhundhu of excessive virility and power, cannot be over-powered completely by any one of insignificant brilliance or even by rulers of the Earth, though they may fight with him for hundreds of years. His prowess and strength is very great, difficult to be approached even by the Devas”.

## \|\| 2.63.46 \|\|

*evamuktastu rājarṣiruttaṅkena mahātmanā \|*  
*kuvalāśvaṃ tu taṃ prādāttasmin dhundhunivāraṇe \|\| 46 \|\|*

46\. On being told thus by the ṇoble-souled Uttaṅka, that saintly king gave him Kuvalāśva for the task of warding off Dhundhu.

## \|\| 2.63.47 \|\|

*bhagavannyastaśasbho 'hamayaṃ tu tanayo mama \|*  
*bhaviṣyati dvijaśreṣṭha dhundhumāro na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

47\. “O holy lord, I have laid down my arms. This is my son, O excellent Brāhmaṇa. He will undoubtedly become the slayer of Dhundhu”.

## \|\| 2.63.48 \|\|

*sa tamādiśya tanayaṃ dhundhumāgṇamacyutam \|*  
*jagāma sa vanāyaiva tapase śaṃsitavrataḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. He ordered his son to carry out the task of slaying Dhunḍhu with any step. The king of praiseworthy holy rites, went to the forest itself for the sake of penance.

## \|\| 2.63.49-51 \|\|

*kuvalāśvastu dharmātmā piturvacanamāśritaḥ \|*  
*sahakrairekaviṃśatyā putrāṇāṃ saha pārthivaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*prāyāduttaṅkasahito dhundhostasya nivāraṇe \|*  
*tamāviśattato viṣṇurbhagavānsvena tejasā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*uttaṅkasya niyogāttu lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā \|*  
*tasminprayāte durdharṣe divi śabdo mahānabhūt \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. Abiding by the order of his father, Kuvalāśva accompanied by his twenty-one thousand sons and Uttaṅka proceeded ahead for resisting Dhundhu. Lord Viṣṇu entered him with his own divine splendour. When, being urged by Uttaṅka and with a desire for the welfare of the world, the unassailable king marched out, there arose a great din and commotion in the sky.

## \|\| 2.63.52 \|\|

*adya prabhṛtyeṣa nṛpo dhundhumāro bhaviṣyati \|*  
*divyaiḥ puṣpaiśca taṃ devāḥ saṃmatātsamavākiran \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. “This king shall become Dhundhumāra (slayer of Dhundhu) with effect from today”: The Devas showered him all round with divine flowers.

## \|\| 2.63.53-55 \|\|

*devadundubhayaścaiva praṇedurhi tadā bhṛśam \|*  
*sa gatvā puruṣavyāghrastanayaiḥ saha vīryavān \|\| 53 \|\|*

*samudraṃ khānayāmāsa vālukāpūrṇamavyayam \|*  
*tasya putraiḥ khanadbhiśca vālukāntarhitastadā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*dhundhurāsāditastatra diśamāśritya paścimām \|*  
*mukhajenāgninā kruddho lokānudvartayanniva \|\| 55 \|\|*

53-55. Then the divine Dundubhis (war-drums) were sounded loudly.

The heroic lion among men went along with his sons and dug up the vast inexhaustible ocean filled with sands. Dhundhu who had concealed himself beneath the sands, was found out by his sons who were digging the sands on the Western side.

That infuriated Asura appeared to upset the worlds by means of fire coming out of his mouth.

## \|\| 2.63.56 \|\|

*vāri susrāva cogena mahodadhirivodaye \|*  
*somasya so 'suraśreṣṭho dhārormikalilo mahān \|\| 56 \|\|*

56\. By means of his Yogic power that great and excellent Asura let flow water like the great ocean blending its currents and waves together at the time of moon-rise.

## \|\| 2.63.57-63 \|\|

*tasya putrāstu nirdagdhāstraya urvaritā mṛdhe \|*  
*tataḥ sa rājātibalo rākṣasaṃ taṃ mahābalam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*āsasāda mahātejā dhundhuṃ bandhunibarhaṇam \|*  
*tasya vārimayaṃ vegamapi vatsa narādhipaḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*yogī yogena vahniṃ ca śamayāmāsa vāriṇā \|*  
*nirasyantaṃ mahākāyaṃ balenodakarākṣasam \|\| 59 \|\|*

*uttaṅkaṃ darśayāmāsa kṛtakarmā narādhipaḥ \|*  
*uttaṅkaśca varaṃ prādāttasmai rājñe mahātmane \|\| 60 \|\|*

*dadataścākṣayaṃ vittaṃ śatrubhiścāpya dhuṣyatām \|*  
*dharme ratiṃ ca satataṃ svarge vāsaṃ tathākṣayam \|\| 61 \|\|*

*putrāṇāṃ cākṣayāṃllokānsvarge ye rakṣasā hatāḥ \|*  
*tasya putrāstrayaḥ śiṣṭā dṛḍhāśvo jyeṣṭha ucyate \|\| 62 \|\|*

*bhadrāśvaḥ kapilāśvaśca kanīyāṃsau tu tau smṛtau \|*  
*dhaindhumārirdṛḍhāśvaśca haryaśvastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

57-60a. All his sons were burnt down completely; only three survived that battle.

Then that king of enormous strength and great splendour approached that immensely mighty Rākṣasa Dhundhu who killed h is kinsmen. The king, O dear one, who was a Yogin, suppressed his forceful flood of water let loose by him my means of his Yogic power and subdued fire by means of water. In the end the king killed that aquatic demon of huge body, by means of his prowess. After accomplishing his task the king pointed the Rākṣasa to Uttaṅka.

60b-63. Uttaṅka granted boon to that noble-souled king that the more he gave as gifts the more would be his wealth ever lasting. The other boons he granted were the invincibility (in battle) by the enemies, perpetual interest in Dharma and never-ending residence in the heaven. He granted the everlasting worlds in heaven to his sons who were killed by the demon.

Out of the three of his sons who survived, the eldest is called Dṛḍhāśva. Bhadrāśva and Kapilāśva are remembered as the younger ones. Dṛḍhāśva is known as Dhaundhumāri (i.e. son of Dhundhumāra) and Haryaśva was his son.

## \|\| 2.63.64 \|\|

*haryaśvasya nikuṃbho 'bhūtkṣātradharmarataḥ sadā \|*  
*saṃhatāśvo nikuṃbhasya suto raṇaviśāradaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Haryaśva’s son was Nikumbha who was always devoted to the duties of a Kṣatriya. Saṃhatāśva, who was an expert in battle, was the son of Nikumbha.

## \|\| 2.63.65-66 \|\|

*kṛśāśvaścākṛtāśvaśca saṃhatāśvasutāvubhau \|*  
*tasya patnī haimavatī satī mātā dṛṣadvatī \|\| 65 \|\|*

*vikhyātā triṣu lokeṣu putraścāsya prasenajit \|*  
*yuvanāśvasutastasya triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

65-66. Kṛśāśva and Akṛtāśva were the two sons of Saṃhatāśva. His wife was the chaste Haimavatī and his mother Dṛṣadvatī was well-known in the three worlds. His (?) son was Prasenajit. Yuvanāśva, his son, was famous in the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.63.67 \|\|

*atyantadhārmikā gaurī tasya patnī pativratā \|*  
*abhiśastā tu sā bhartrā nadī sā bāhudā kṛtā \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. His wife Gaurī was an extremely virtuous and chaste lady. But she was cursed by her husband and was converted into the river Bāhudā.

## \|\| 2.63.68 \|\|

*tasyāstu gaurikaḥ putraścakravartī babhūva ha \|*  
*māndhātā yauvanāśvo vai trailokyavijayī nṛpaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. Her son Gaurika (i.e. son of Gaurī) became an emperor. Māndhātṛ, the son of Yuvanāśva, was a king who conquered the three worlds.

## \|\| 2.63.69-72 \|\|

*atrāpyudāharantīmaṃ ślokaṃ paurāṇikā dvijāḥ \|*  
*yāvatsūrya udayate yāvacca pratitiṣṭhati \|\| 69 \|\|*

*sarvaṃ tadyauvanāśvasya māndhātuḥ kṣetramucyate \|*  
*tasya caitrarathī bhāryā śaśabindoḥ sutābhavat \|\| 70 \|\|*

*sādhvī bindumatī nāma rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi \|*  
*pativratā ca jyeṣṭhā ca bhātṝṇāmayutasya sā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tasyāmutpādayāmāsa māndhātā trīnsutanprabhuḥ \|*  
*purukutsamaṃbarīṣaṃ mucukundaṃ ca viśrutam \|\| 72 \|\|*

69-72. In this context the Brāhmaṇas well-versed in the Purāṇas cite the following stanza:—

The entire space where the sun rises and establishes itself is called the territory of Māndhātā, son of Yuvanāśva.

His wife was the daughter of Citraratha (?) and Śaśabindu. She was a chaste lady named Bindumatī. In beauty she was unrivalled on the Earth. This chaste lady was the eldest sister of ten thousand brothers. Lord Māndhātā begot of her three sons viz. Purukutsa, Arnbarīṣa and Mucukunda who was well-known.

## \|\| 2.63.73 \|\|

*aṃbarīṣasya dāyādo yuvanāśvo 'paraḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*narmadāyāṃ samutpannaḥ saṃbhūtastasya cātmajaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Another Yuvanāśva is remembered as the heir of Ambarīṣa. He was born of Narmadā. Sambhūta was his son.

## \|\| 2.63.74 \|\|

*saṃbhūtasyātmajaḥ putro ṅyanaraṇyaḥ pratāpavān \|*  
*rāvaṇena hato yena trailokyaṃ vijitaṃ purā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. The valorous Anaraṇya was the bosom-born son of Sambhūta. He was killed by Rāvaṇa by whom all the three worlds had been conquered before.

## \|\| 2.63.75 \|\|

*tena dṛśyonaraṇyasya haryaśvastasya cātmajaḥ \|*  
*haryaśvāttu dṛṣadvatyāṃ jajñe ca sumatirnṛpaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. (Defective text) Tenadṛśya (?) (prob. Trasadasyu) was the son of Anaraṇya. Haryaśva was Trasadasyu’s son. King Sumati was born of Dṛṣadvatī and Haryaśva.)

## \|\| 2.63.76 \|\|

*tasya putro 'bhavadrājā tridhanvā nāma dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*āsīttridhanvanaścāpi vidvāṃstrayyāruṇiḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

76\. His son was a virtuous king named Tridhanvā. The son of Tridhanvā was the scholarly lord Trayyāruṇi.

## \|\| 2.63.77-79 \|\|

*tasya satyavrato nāma kumāro 'bhūnmahābalaḥ \|*  
*tena bhāryā vidarbhasya tdṛtā hatvā divaukasaḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*pāṇigrahaṇamantreṣu niṣṭānaṃ prāpiteṣviha \|*  
*kāmādbalācca mohācca saṃharṣeṇa balena ca \|\| 78 \|\|*

*bhāvinor'thasya ca balāttatkṛtaṃ tena dhīmatā \|*  
*tamadharmeṇa saṃyuktaṃ pitā bhayyāruṇo 'tyajat \|\| 79 \|\|*

77-79. A son of great strength named Satyavrata was born to him. After killing the heaven-dwellers (?), Vidrabha’s wife was abducted by him. This sin was committed by that intelligent one out of lust, strength and great delight, forcibly out of delusion and due to the power of the inevitable future. This was done by him when the Mantras of the wedding ceremony had not been concluded. His father Trayyāruṇa banished him because he had been sinful.

## \|\| 2.63.80-81 \|\|

*apadhvaṃseti bahuśo vadankrodhasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*pitaraṃ so 'bravīdekaḥ kva gacchāmīti vai muhuḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*pitā cainamathovāca śvapākaiḥ saha varttaya \|*  
*nāhaṃ putreṇa putrārthī tvayādya kulapāṃsana \|\| 81 \|\|*

80-81. Becoming infuriated with him, he exclaimed many times “This is disgrace and degradation”.

He asked his father again and again, “I am alone. Where shall I go?”.

The father told him, “Go and. live along with Cāṇḍālas, O defiler of the family. With you as my son, I am not a seeker of a son now. Although I seek sons, they should not be like you”.

## \|\| 2.63.82 \|\|

*ityuktaḥ sa nirākrāmannagarādvacanā dvibhoḥ \|*  
*na cainaṃ vārayāmāsa vasiṣṭho bhagavānṛṣiḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. On being told thus, he went out of the city at the instance of the lord, the king. Vasiṣṭha, the exalted sage, did not prevent him from going.

## \|\| 2.63.83 \|\|

*sa tu satyavrato dhīmāñśvapākāvasathāntike \|*  
*pitrā tyakto 'vasaddhīraḥ pitā cāsya vanaṃ yayau \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. Satyavrata who was intelligent and bold, lived near the abodes of Cāṇḍālas on being abandoned by his father. His father went to the forest.

## \|\| 2.63.84 \|\|

*tasmiṃstu viṣaye tasya nāvarṣatpākaśāsanaḥ \|*  
*samā dvādaśa saṃpūrmāstenādharmeṇa vai tadā \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. On account of this sin, Indra did not shower rain in that country for full twelve years.

## \|\| 2.63.85 \|\|

*dārāṃstu tasya viṣaye viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ \|*  
*saṃnyasya sāgarānūpe cacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Viśvāmitra, a sage of great penance, left his wife in the territory of that king and performed extensive penance in the marshy shores of the Sea.

## \|\| 2.63.86 \|\|

*tasya patnī gale baddhvā madhyamaṃputramaurasam \|*  
*śiṣṭānāṃ bharaṇārthāya vyakrīṇādgośatena vai \|\| 86 \|\|*

86\. His wife tied her own bosom-born middle son with a rope round his neck and offered him for sale in exchange for a hundred cows. She wanted to sell him in order to sustain and bring up the remaining sons.

## \|\| 2.63.87-88 \|\|

*taṃ tu baddhaṃ gale dṛṣṭavā vikrayārthaṃ narottamaḥ \|*  
*maharṣiputraṃ dharmātmā mokṣayāmāsa suvrataḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*satyavrato mahābuddhirbharaṇaṃ tasya cākarot \|*  
*viśvāmitrasya tuṣṭyarthamanukaṃpārthameva ca \|\| 88 \|\|*

87-88. The excellent king of holy rites and virtuous soul saw the son of the great sage tied round the neck and offered for sale. Thereupon, he released him.

For the sake of satisfying Viśvāmitra and arousing his sympathy, Satyavrata, of great intellect, sustained him and brought him up too.

## \|\| 2.63.89 \|\|

*so 'bhavadgālavo nāma gale baddho mahātapāḥ \|*  
*maharṣiḥ kauśikastāta tena vīreṇa mokṣitaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

89\. That boy who had been tied round the neck became a sage of great penance named Gālava. That Kauśika (one belonging to the family of Kuśika) was redeemed by that heroic king.

## \|\| 2.63.90 \|\|

*tasya vratena bhaktyā ca kṛpayā ca pratijñayā \|*  
*viśvāmitrakalatraṃ ca babhāra vinaye sthitaḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

90\. On account of his (?) holy vow, devotion, mercy and solemn declaration, the king who adhered to rules of discipline, sustained Viśvāmitra’s wife also.

## \|\| 2.63.91 \|\|

*hatvā mṛgānvarāhāṃśca mahiṣāṃśca jalecarān \|*  
*viśvāmitrāśramābhyāse tanmāṃsamanayattataḥ \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. He used to kill deer, boars, buffaloes and aquatic beings and bring their meat near the hermitage of Viśvāmitra.

## \|\| 2.63.92-93 \|\|

*upāṃśuvratamāsthāya dīkṣāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm \|*  
*piturniyogādabhajannṛpe tu vanamāsthite \|\| 92 \|\|*

*ayodhyāṃ caiva rāṣṭraṃ ca tathaivāntaḥ puraṃ puniḥ \|*  
*yājyotthānyāyasaṃyogādvasiṣṭhaḥ paryarakṣata \|\| 93 \|\|*

92-93. At the instance of sage Vasiṣṭha Satyavrata’s father undertook Upāṃśuvrata (a secret vow) and for that purpose took initiation extending to twelve years. When the king went to the forest, Vasiṣṭha protected Ayodhyā, the harem and the whole realm from the evil contact and injustice arising from Satya-vrata.

## \|\| 2.63.94 \|\|

*satyavrataḥ subālyāttu bhāvinor'thasya vai balāt \|*  
*vasiṣṭhe 'bhyadhikaṃ manyuṃ dhārayāmāsa manyunā \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. On account of his childishness as well as due to the force of inevitable future, Satyavrata bore a grudge against Vasiṣṭha due to grief.

## \|\| 2.63.95 \|\|

*pitrā tu taṃ tadā rāṣṭrātparityaktaṃ svamātmajam \|*  
*na vārayāmāsa munirvasiṣṭhaḥ kāraṇena vai \|\| 95 \|\|*

95\. When Satyavrata was banished from the realm by the father, Sage Vasiṣṭha did not prevent this, due to a specific reason.

## \|\| 2.63.96 \|\|

*pāṇigrahamamantrāṇāṃ niṣṭhā syātsaptame pade \|*  
*evaṃ satyavratastāṃ vai hṛtavānsaptame pade \|\| 96 \|\|*

96\. The conclusion of the wedding Mantras shall be only at the seventh step (Saptapadi). Thinking thus Satyavrata abducted her (?) at the seventh step.

## \|\| 2.63.97 \|\|

*jānandharmānvasiṣṭhastu navamantrānihecchati \|*  
*iti satyavrato roṣaṃ vasiṣṭhe manasākarot \|\| 97 \|\|*

97\. “Despite being conversant with Dharmas, Vasiṣṭha wishes for fresh chanting of the Mantras”,—saying thus Satyavrata became angry with Vasiṣṭha, in his mind.

## \|\| 2.63.98 \|\|

*guṇabuddhyā tu bhagavānvasiṣṭhaḥ kṛtavāṃstapaḥ \|*  
*na tu satyavrato 'budhyadupāṃśuvratamasya vai \|\| 98 \|\|*

98\. The Saintly lord Vasiṣṭha performed penance for their welfare. But Satyavratra did not understand his secret vow.

## \|\| 2.63.99 \|\|

*tasmiṃstu paramo roṣaḥ piturāsīnmahātmanaḥ \|*  
*tena dvādaśa varṣāṇi nāvarṣatpākaśāsanaḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. The fury of his noble-souled father was excessively directed to his son. Therefore, Indra did not shower rain for twelve years.

## \|\| 2.63.100-101 \|\|

*tena tvidānīṃ vahatā dīkṣāṃ tāṃ durvahāṃ bhuvi \|*  
*kulasya niṣkṛtiḥ svasya sṛteyaṃ ca bhavediti \|\| 100 \|\|*

*tato vasiṣṭho bhagavānpitrā tyaktaṃ na vārayat \|*  
*abhiṣekṣyāmyahaṃ naṣṭe paścādenamiti prabhuḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

100-101. “Atonement can be made in the family by me if I take up initiation which is very difficult to undertake on the earth now”. So thought Vasiṣṭha. He did not prevent the banishment of the son by the father thinking thus—“when he passes away, I shall crown him”. In the meantime that king of potentiality undertook initiation extending to twelve years.

## \|\| 2.63.102-103 \|\|

*sa tu dvādaśavarṣāṇi dīkṣāṃ tāmudvahanbalī \|*  
*avidyamāne māṃse tu vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ \|\| 102 \|\|*

*sarvakāmadughāṃ dhenuṃ sa dadarśa nṛpātmajaḥ \|*  
*tāṃ vai krodhācca mohācca śramaccaiva kṣudhānvitaḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

102-103. When there was no meat readily available, the son of the king espied the divine cow of the noble-souled Vasiṣṭha that milked everyone of desires of devotees.

The most excellent one among powerful ones, who was hungry due to fatigue, adopted the policy of thieves and killed the cow on account of his anger (towards Vasiṣṭha) and delusion too. He himself made the sons of Viśvāmitra eat the meat. On hearing about it, Vasiṣṭha cast him off. The holy lord Vasiṣṭha said thus to the prince.

## \|\| 2.63.104-108 \|\|

*dasyudharmagato dṛṣṭvā jaghāna balināṃ varaḥ \|*  
*satu māṃsaṃ svayaṃ caiva viśvāmitrasya cātmajān \|\| 104 \|\|*

*bhojayāmāsa tacchrutvā vasiṣṭhastaṃ tadātyajat \|*  
*provāca caiva bhagavānvasiṣṭhastaṃ nṛpātmajam \|\| 105 \|\|*

*pātayeyamahaṃ krūra tava śaṅkuma pohya vai \|*  
*yadi te trīṇi śaṅkūni na syurhi puruṣādhama \|\| 106 \|\|*

*pituścāpāritoṣeṇa gurordegadhrīvadhena ca \|*  
*aprokṣitopayogācca trividhaste vyatikramaḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

*evaṃ sa trīṇi śaṅkūni dṛṣṭvā tasya mahātapāḥ \|*  
*triśaṅkuriti hovāca triśaṅkustena sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 108 \|\|*

104-108. “If you had not already had three sins, O base one among men, I would have made you fall down, O cruel one, after inflicting another sin.

You have committed sins in three ways viz.—“You made your father dissatisfied, you killed the cow of your preceptor, you made use of what had not been sacrificed by the sprinkling of holy water.”

Thus the sage of great power of penance saw the three sins (Śaṅkus) and called him Triśaṅku. Therefore, the king is remembered as Triśaṅku.

## \|\| 2.63.109-112 \|\|

*viśvāmitrastu dārāṇāmāgato bharaṇe kṛte \|*  
*tatastasmai varaṃ prādāttadā prītastriśaṅkave \|\| 109 \|\|*

*chandyamāno vareṇātha guruṃ vavrenṛpātmajaḥ \|*  
*saśarīro vraje svargamityevaṃ yācito varaḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

*anāvṛṣṭibhaye tasmiñjāte dvādaśavārṣike \|*  
*abhiṣicya rājye pitrye yojayāmāsa taṃ muniḥ \|\| 111 \|\|*

*miṣatāṃ devatānāṃ ca vasiṣṭhasya ca kauśikaḥ \|*  
*saśarīraṃ tadā taṃ vai divamāropayatprabhuḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

109-112. Viśvāmitra who returned (from his penance) became delighted with Triśaṅku because he had sustained his wife (during the absence of the sage). He granted him a boon. When he was pressed to choose a boon the prince chose him as his preceptor and requested for this boon—“I shall go to heaven along with this physical body.” When there was a danger of draught extending to twelve years, the sage crowned him in his hereditary kingdom. Even as the Devas as well as Vasiṣṭha were watching, the lordly saint Viśvāmitra made him ascend heaven.

## \|\| 2.63.113-114 \|\|

*miṣatastu vasiṣṭhasya tadadbhutamivābhavat \|*  
*atrāpyudāharantīmaṃ ślokaṃ paurāṇikā janāḥ \|\| 113 \|\|*

*viśvāmitraprasādena triśaṅkurdivirājate \|*  
*devaiḥ sārddhaṃ mahātejānugrahāttasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

113-114. It was all the more surprising because it happened even as Vasiṣṭha was watching. In this context persons well-versed in the Purāṇas cite this stanza:

“Due to Viśvāmitra’s favour and on account of the blessing of that intelligent sage, Triśaṅku of great splendour shines in heaven alone with the Devas.

## \|\| 2.63.115 \|\|

*tasya satyaratā nāma bhāryā kaikayavaṃśajā \|*  
*kumāraṃ janayāmāsa hariścandramakalmaṣam \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. His wife named Satyavratā, born of the family of Kaikeyas, gave birth to Hariścandra, a sinless son.

## \|\| 2.63.116 \|\|

*sa tu rājā hariścandrastraiśaṅkava iti śrutaḥ \|*  
*ahartā rājasūyasya samraḍiti pariśrutaḥ \|\| 116 \|\|*

116\. King Hariścandra is well known as Traiśaṅkava (son of Triśaṅku). As a performer of Rājasūya sacrifice, he became famous as an Emperor.

## \|\| 2.63.117 \|\|

*hariścandrasya tu suto rohito nāma vīryavān \|*  
*harito rohitasyātha cañcurharīta ucyate \|\| 117 \|\|*

117\. Hariścandra had a heroic and powerful son named Rohita. Harita was the son of Rohita and Cañcu is mentioned as the son of Harita.

## \|\| 2.63.118 \|\|

*vinayaśca sudevaśca cañcuputrau babhūvatuḥ \|*  
*caitā sarvasya kṣatrasya vijayastena sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

118\. Vinaya and Sudeva were the two sons of Cañcu. Sudeva was the conqueror of all Kṣatriyas. Hence, he is remembered as Vijaya.

## \|\| 2.63.119 \|\|

*rurukastanayastasya rājā dharmārthakovidaḥ \|*  
*rurukāttu vṛkaḥ putrastasmādbāhurvijajñivān \|\| 119 \|\|*

119\. Ruruka was his son. He was a king proficient in details regarding Dharma and Wealth (Artha). Vṛka was the son of Ruruka and Bāhu was born of him.

## \|\| 2.63.120 \|\|

*haihayaistālajaṅghaiśca nirasto vyasanī nṛpaḥ \|*  
*śakairyavanakāṃbojaiḥ pāradaiḥ pahlavaistathā \|\| 120 \|\|*

120\. Since that king indulged in vice, he was dethroned by the Haihayas, Tālajaṅghas, Śakas, Yavanas, Kāmbojas, Pāradas and Pahlavas.

## \|\| 2.63.121 \|\|

*nātyarthaṃ dhārmiko 'bhūtsa dharmye sati yuge tathā \|*  
*sagarastu suto bāhorjajñe saha gareṇa vai \|\| 121 \|\|*

121\. Even when the Yuga was conducive to the development of virtue, that king was not much of a righteous person. Sagara was the son of Bāhu. He was born along with poison.

## \|\| 2.63.122-123 \|\|

*bhṛgorāśramamāsādya hyaurvaiṇa parirakṣitaḥ \|*  
*agneyamastraṃ labdhvā tu bhārgavātsagaro nṛpaḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

*jaghāna pṛthivīṃ gatvā tālajaṅghānsahaihayān \|*  
*śakānāṃ pahlavānāṃ ca dharmaṃ nirasadacyutaḥ \|\| 123 \|\|*

122-123. It was at the hermitage of Bhṛgu that he was born. He was protected by Aurva. After acquiring the Āgneya Astra (a missile the deity of which is fire-god) from the grandson of Bḥrgu (viz. Aurva) king Sagara went over the whole of the Earth and killed Tālajaṅghas and Haihayas. The unerring king repudiated the Dharma (code of conduct etc.) of the Śakas and Pahlavas.

## \|\| 2.63.124-125 \|\|

*kṣatriyāṇāṃ tathā teṣāṃ pāradānāṃ ca dharmavit \|*  
*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*kathaṃ sa sagaro rājā gareṇa saha jajñivān \|\| 124 \|\|*

*kimarthaṃ vā śakādīnāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ mahaujasām \|*  
*dharmānkulocitānkruddho rājā nirasadacyutaḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

124-125. (Sagara) who was conversant with the real Dharma cast out the Dharma of the Kṣatriyas called (Pāradas) i.e. excommunicated them from Kṣatriya-hooḍ.

The sages enquired:—

How was the king Sagara born along with poison? What for did the infuriated king who never committed a fault banish them from the hereditary and traditional codes of conduct of Śakas and others who were Kṣatriyas of great prowess?

Sūta explained:—

## \|\| 2.63.126 \|\|

*suta uvāca*  
*bāhorvyasaninastasya tdṛtaṃ rājyaṃ purā kila \|*  
*haihayaistālajaṅghaiśca śakaiḥ sārddhaṃ samāgataiḥ \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. It has already been mentioned that the kingdom of Bāhu who indulged in vice, had been formerly seized by the Haihayas and Tālajaṅghas who came along with the Śakas.

## \|\| 2.63.127 \|\|

*yavanāḥ pāradāścaiva kāṃbojāḥ pahlavāstathā \|*  
*haihayārthaṃ parākrāntā ete pañca gaṇāstadā \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. The Yavanas, Pāraḍas, Kāmbojas. Pahlavas (and śakas), these five clans (of kings) attacked for and on behalf of the Haihayas.

## \|\| 2.63.128 \|\|

*tdṛtarājyastadābāhuḥ saṃnyasya sa tadā gṛham \|*  
*vanaṃ praviśya dharmātmā saha patnyā tapo 'carat \|\| 128 \|\|*

128\. When he had been deprived of his kingdom, Bāhu renounced his abode and entered the forest. Accompanied by h is wife, the noble-souled king performed a penance.

## \|\| 2.63.129 \|\|

*kadācidapyakalpaḥ sa toyārthaṃ prasthito nṛpaḥ \|*  
*vṛddhatvāddurbalatvācca hyantarā sa mamāra ca \|\| 129 \|\|*

129\. Once that king, though disabled, went to fetch water. On account of old age and weakness, he passed away in. the middle.

## \|\| 2.63.130 \|\|

*patnī tu yādavī tasya sagarbhā pṛṣṭhato 'pyagāt \|*  
*sapatnyā tu garastasyai datto garbhajighāṃsayā \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. His wife, a member of the family of Yadu, was pregnant and she had gone after him. Poison had been administered to her by her co-wife with a desire to kill the child in the womb.

## \|\| 2.63.131 \|\|

*sā tu bhartuścitāṃ kṛtvā vahniṃ taṃ samārohayat \|*  
*aurvastaṃ bhārgavo dṛṣṭvā kāruṇyāddhi nyavarttayat \|\| 131 \|\|*

131\. She lit the funeral pyre of her husband and got on to it. On seeing her, Aurva, the grand-son of Bḥṭgu, made her desist from it out of mercy.

## \|\| 2.63.132 \|\|

*tasyāśrame tu garbhaṃ sā gareṇa ca tadā saha \|*  
*vyajāyata mahābāhuṃ sagaraṃ nāma dharmikam \|\| 132 \|\|*

132\. She gave birth to the child developed in her womb along with the poison. She gave birth to a righteous son named Sagara who became very powerful.

## \|\| 2.63.133 \|\|

*aurvastu jātakarmādīnkṛtvā tasya mahātmanaḥ \|*  
*adhyāpya vedāñchāstrāṇi tato 'straṃ pratyapādayat \|\| 133 \|\|*

133\. Aurva performed Jātakarman and other post-natal holy rites of the noble-souled prince. He taught him Vedas and Sacred scriptures. Thereafter, he taught him how to discharge missiles and miraculous weapons.

## \|\| 2.63.134 \|\|

*tataḥ śakānsa yavanānkāṃbojānpāradāṃstathā \|*  
*pahlavāṃścaiva niḥśeṣānkartuṃ vyavasito nṛpaḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

134\. After that the king determined to exterminate the Śakas, Yavanas, Kāmbojas, Pāradas, and Pahlavas.

## \|\| 2.63.135 \|\|

*te hanyamānā vīreṇa sagareṇa mahātmanā \|*  
*vasiṣṭhaṃ śaraṇaṃ sarve saṃprāptāḥ śaraṇaiṣiṇaḥ \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. On being hit, hurt and killed by the noble-souled, heroic Sagara, all of them sought refuge in Vasiṣṭha, desirous of shelter.

## \|\| 2.63.136 \|\|

*vasiṣṭho vīkṣya tānyuktānvinayona mahāmuniḥ \|*  
*sagaraṃ vārayāmāsa teṣāṃ dattvābhayaṃ tathā \|\| 136 \|\|*

136\. On seeing them filled with humility, the great sage granted them freedom from fear and restrained Sagara.

## \|\| 2.63.137 \|\|

*sagaraḥ svāṃ pratijñāṃ ca gurorvākyaṃ niśamya ca \|*  
*jaghāna dharmaṃ vai teṣāṃ veṣānyatvaṃ cakāra ha \|\| 137 \|\|*

137\. Remembering his own vow and on hearing the prescriptive words of; his preceptor, Sagara struck off their customary observances of caste and other characteristics, and made them change their guise and garments.

## \|\| 2.63.138-139 \|\|

*arddhaṃ śākānāṃ śiraso muṇḍayitvā vyasarjayat \|*  
*yavanānāṃ śiraḥ sarvaṃ kāṃbojānāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 138 \|\|*

*pāradā muktakeśāśca pahlavāḥ śmaśrudhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*niḥsvādhyāyavaṣaṭkārāḥ kṛtāstena mahātmanā \|\| 139 \|\|*

138-139. He shaved half of the heads of Śakas and discharged them. He shaved off the heads of Yavanas and Kāmbojas completely. The Pāradas were compelled to keep their hairs dishevelled and the Pahlavas were made to grow their moustache and beard. All of them were deprived of the study of the Vedas and the utterance of the Vaṣaṭkāra Mantras, by that noble-souled king.

## \|\| 2.63.140-141 \|\|

*śakā yavana kāṃbojāḥ pahlavāḥ pāradaiḥ saha \|*  
*kalisparśā mahiṣikā dārvascholāḥ khaśāstathā \|\| 140 \|\|*

*sarve te kṣatriyagaṇā dharmasteṣāṃ nirākṛtaḥ \|*  
*vasiṣṭhavacanātpūrvaṃ sagareṇa mahātmanā \|\| 141 \|\|*

140-141. The Śakas, Yavanas, Kāmbojas, Pahlavas, Pāradas, Kalisparśas, Māhiṣikas, Dārvas, Colas and Khaśas—the customary observations of their castes and conventions of all these groups of Kṣatriyas were prohibited formerly by the noble-souled Sagara at the instance of Vasiṣṭha.

## \|\| 2.63.142 \|\|

*sa dharmavijayī rājā vijityemāṃ vasundharām \|*  
*aśvaṃ vai cārayāmāsa vājimedhāya dīkṣitaḥ \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. After conquering the whole of the Earth by means of righteous victory, the king took initiation for the horse sacrifice and made the sacrificial horse go round the world.

## \|\| 2.63.143 \|\|

*tasya cārayataḥ so 'śvaḥ samudre pūrvadakṣiṇe \|*  
*velāsamīpe 'pahṛto bhūmiṃ caiva praveśitaḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

143\. As he made it go round, the horse was stolen away near the shore of the South-Eastern Ocean and made to enter beneath the earth.

## \|\| 2.63.144-145 \|\|

*sa taṃ deśaṃ sutaiḥ sarvaiḥ khānayāmāsa pārthivaḥ \|*  
*āseduśca tatastasminkhanantaste mahārmave \|\| 144 \|\|*

*tamādipuruṣaṃ devaṃ hariṃ kṛṣṇaṃ prajāpatim \|*  
*viṣṇuṃ kapilarūpeṇa haṃsaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum \|\| 145 \|\|*

144-145. The king got that place completely dug up by his sons. Digging up the bed of the great ocean, they met with the primordial being, Lord Viṣṇu. in the form of Kapila, the lord Hari, Kṛṣṇa, the lord of subjects, lord Haṃsa, lord Nārāyaṇa.

## \|\| 2.63.146 \|\|

*tasya cakṣuḥ samāsādya tejastatpratipadyate \|*  
*dagdhāḥ putrāstadā sarvecatvārastvavaśeṣitāḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

146\. After coming within the path of his vision and being afflicted by its fiery splendour, all those princes were burned; only four sons survived.

## \|\| 2.63.147 \|\|

*barhiketuḥ suketuśca tathā dharmarathaśca yaḥ \|*  
*śūraḥ pañcajanaścaiva tasya vaṃśakarāḥ prabhoḥ \|\| 147 \|\|*

147\. They were Barhiketu, Suketu, Dharmaratha and the heroic Pañcajana. They perpetuated the line of the lord.

## \|\| 2.63.148-150 \|\|

*prādācca tasya bhagavānharirnārāyaṇo varān \|*  
*akṣayatvaṃ svavaṃśasya vājimedhaśataṃ tathā \|\| 148 \|\|*

*vibhuḥ putraṃ samudraṃ ca svarge vāsaṃ tathākṣayam \|*  
*taṃ samudro 'śvamādāya vavande saritāṃpatiḥ \|\| 149 \|\|*

*sāgaratvaṃ ca lebhe sa karmaṇā tena tasya vai \|*  
*taṃ cāśvamedhikaṃ so 'śvaṃ samudrātprāpya pārthivaḥ \|\| 150 \|\|*

148-150. Hari, Nārāyaṇa granted him boons viz—everlasting status to his race, ability to perform hundred horse sacrifices, the all pervading ocean as a son, and the eternal residence in heaven.

Fetching the horse with him, the ocean, the lord of rivers, saluted him. By that activity of his, he got the name Sāgara.

After getting back the sacrificial horse from the ocean, the king performed horse-sacrifices again and again making up the total of one hundred.

## \|\| 2.63.151-152 \|\|

*ājahārāśvamedhānāṃ śataṃ caiva punaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*ṣaṣṭiṃ putrasahasrāṇi dagdhānyasya ruṣā vibho \|\| 151 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ nārāyaṇaṃ tejaḥ praviṣṭāni mahātmanām \|*  
*putrāṇāṃ tu sahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭistu iti naḥ śrutam \|\| 152 \|\|*

151-152. His sixty thousand sons were burned by the anger of the lord Kapila. We have heard that the noble-souled sixty thousand sons entered the brilliant lustre of Nārāyaṇa.

The Sages asked:—

## \|\| 2.63.153 \|\|

*ṛṣaya ūcuḥ*  
*sagarasyātmajā nānā kathaṃ jātā mahābalāḥ \|*  
*vikrāntāḥ ṣaṣṭisāhasrā vidhinā kena vā vada \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. Tell us by what procedure were the numerous, highly mighty and valorous sons of Sagara, sixty thousand in number were born.

Sūta replied:—

## \|\| 2.63.154 \|\|

*suta uvāca*  
*dvepatnyau sagarasyāstāṃ tapasā dagadhakilbiṣe \|*  
*jyeṣṭhā vidarbhaduhitā keśinī nāma nāmataḥ \|\| 154 \|\|*

154\. Sagara had two wives who had dispelled their sins by means of their penance. The elder of the two was the daughter of Vidarbha named Keśinī.

## \|\| 2.63.155 \|\|

*kanīyasī tu yā tasyapatnī paramadharmiṇī \|*  
*ariṣṭanemiduhitā rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi \|\| 155 \|\|*

155\. His younger wife was the daughter of Ariṣṭanemī. She was extremely virtuous and unparalleled in beauty throughout the world.

## \|\| 2.63.156-160 \|\|

*aurvastābhyāṃ varaṃ prādāttapasārādhitaḥ prabhuḥ \|*  
*ekā janiṣyate putraṃ vaṃśakarttāramīpsitam \|\| 156 \|\|*

*ṣaṣṭiṃ putrasahasrāṇi dvitīyā janayiṣyati \|*  
*munestu vacanaṃ śrutvā keśinī putramekakam \|\| 157 \|\|*

*vaṃśasya kāraṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jagrāha nṛpa saṃsadi \|*  
*ṣaṣṭiṃ putrasahasrāṇi suparṇabhaginī tathā \|\| 158 \|\|*

*mahābhāgā pramuditā jagrāha sumatistathā \|*  
*atha kāle gate jyeṣṭhā jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ vyajāyata \|\| 159 \|\|*

*asamañja iti khyātaṃ kākutsthaṃ sagarātmajam \|*  
*sumatistvapi jajñe vai garbhatuṃbaṃ yaśasvinī \|\| 160 \|\|*

156-159a. On being propitiated by means of austerities, the lordly sage Aurva granted them these boons viz.—One of them would give birth to a desired son who would perpetuate the line and the second would give birth to sixty thousand sons.

On hearing the words of the sage, Keśinī chose the single excellent son who would perpetuate the line, O king, in the assembly. Sumati, the sister of Suparṇa, of exalted good fortune, delightedly chose the sixty thousand sons.

159b-160. As time passed on, the eider queen gave birth to the eldest son of Sagara well known by the name of Asamañja, the scion of the family of Kakutstha. Sumati of great renown gave birth to a pot-gourd like the lump of foetus.

## \|\| 2.63.161 \|\|

*ṣaṣṭiḥ putrasahasrāṇāṃ tuṃbamadhyādvinissṛtāḥ \|*  
*ghṛtapūrṇeṣu kuṃbheṣu tāngarbhānyadadhāttataḥ \|\| 161 \|\|*

161\. The sixty thousand sons emerged from the gourdlike lump of foetus. He then placed them (the pieces of the foetus) in the pot filled with ghee.

## \|\| 2.63.162-163 \|\|

*dhātrīścaikaikaśaḥ prādāttāvatīḥ poṣaṇe nṛpaḥ \|*  
*tato navasu māseṣu samuttasthuryathāsukham \|\| 162 \|\|*

*kumārāste mahābhāgāḥ sagaraprītivarddhanāḥ \|*  
*kālena mahātā caiva yaivanaṃ samupāśritāḥ \|\| 163 \|\|*

162-163. The king engaged as many nurses (as there were pieces) in. order to nurture them individually. Thereafter, in nine months, all those sons of exalted fortune fully developed comfortably increasing the pleasure of Sagara. After a long time, they entered the prime of youth.

## \|\| 2.63.164-165 \|\|

*keśinyāstanayo yo 'nyaḥ sagarasyātmasaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*asamañja iti khyāto varhiketurmahābalaḥ \|\| 164 \|\|*

*paurāṇāmahite yuktaḥ pitrā nirvāsitaḥ purāt \|*  
*tasya putroṃ'śumānnāma asamañjasya vīryavān \|\| 165 \|\|*

164-165. The other son of Sagara born of Keśinī was Barhiketu of great strength well known as Asamañja. Since he was engaged against the interests of citizens, he was banished from the city by his father. The heroic son of Asamañja was named Aṃśumān.

## \|\| 2.63.166 \|\|

*tasya putrastu dharmātmā dilīpa iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*dilīpāttu mahātejā vīro jāto bhagīrathaḥ \|\| 166 \|\|*

166\. His noble-souled son was well known as Dilīpa. Bhagīratha, a hero of great splendour, was born of Dilīpa.

## \|\| 2.63.167 \|\|

*yena gaṅgā saricchreṣṭhā vimānairupaśobhitā \|*  
*ihānītā sureśādvai duhitṛtve ca kalpitā \|\| 167 \|\|*

167\. It was by him that Gaṅgā, the most excellent of all rivers, rendered splendid by aerial chariots, was brought here (in this world) and assigned the status of his daughter by the lord of Suras (Brahmā).

## \|\| 2.63.168-169 \|\|

*atrāpyudāharantīmaṃ ślokaṃ paurāṇikā janāḥ \|*  
*bhagīrathastu tāṃ gaṅgāmānayāmāsa karmabhiḥ \|\| 168 \|\|*

*tasmādbhāgīrathī gaṅgā kathyate vaṃśavittamaiḥ \|*  
*bhagīrathasutaścāpi śruto nāma babhūvaha \|\| 169 \|\|*

168-169. In this context, persons well-versed in the Purāṇas cite this verse. “By means of his active endeavour Bhagīratha brought Gaṅgā to the Earth. Hence Gaṅgā is called Bhāgīrathī by those excellent persons who are conversant with genealogy.” Bhagīratha’s son was named Śruta.

## \|\| 2.63.170 \|\|

*nābhāgastasya dāyādo nityaṃ dharmaparāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*ambarīṣaḥ sutastasya siṃdhudvīpastato 'bhavat \|\| 170 \|\|*

170\. Nābhāga was his heir. He was always engaged in virtuous activities. Ambarīṣa was his son and Sindhudvīpa was the next king.

## \|\| 2.63.171-172 \|\|

*pūrve vaṃśapurāṇajñā gāyantīti pariśrutam \|*  
*nābhāgeraṃbarīṣasya bhujābhyāṃ paripālitā \|\| 171 \|\|*

*babhūva vasudhātyarthaṃ tāpatrayavivarjitā \|*  
*ayutāyuḥ sutastasya siṃdhudvīpasya vīryavān \|\| 172 \|\|*

171-172. It is well known that persons of yore conversant with the Purāṇas and genealogy sing thus:—‘The Earth protected by the arms of Ambarīṣa, son of Nābhāga became perfectly free from the three distresses”. Ayutāyu was the heroic son of Sindhudvīpa.

## \|\| 2.63.173 \|\|

*ayutāyostu dāyāda ṛtuparṇo mahāyaśāḥ \|*  
*divyākṣahṛdayajño 'sau rājā nalasakho balī \|\| 173 \|\|*

173\. Ṛtuparṇa of great renown was the heir of Ayutāyu. This strong king who was conversant with the divine Mantra Akṣahṛdaya (the heart of dice) was a friend of Nala.

## \|\| 2.63.174 \|\|

*nalau dvāviti vikhyātau purāṇeṣu dṛḍhavratau \|*  
*vīrasenātmajaścaiva yaścekṣvākukulodvahaḥ \|\| 174 \|\|*

174\. Two Nalas of steadfast holy vows are well known in the Purāṇas: the one, the son of Vīrasena and the other the prominent member of the family of Ikṣvāku.

## \|\| 2.63.175 \|\|

*ṛtuparṇasya putro 'bhūtsarvakāmo janeśvaraḥ \|*  
*sudāsastasya tanayo rājā indrasakho 'bhavat \|\| 175 \|\|*

175\. Sarvakāma, the lord of the people, was the son of Ṛtuparṇa. King Sudāsa, his son, became a friend of Indra.

## \|\| 2.63.176 \|\|

*sudāsasya sutaḥ proktaḥ saudāso nāma pārthivaḥ \|*  
*khyātaḥ kalmāṣapādo vai nāmnā sitrasahaśca saḥ \|\| 176 \|\|*

176\. Sudāsa’s son, the king named Saudāsa became well-known as Kalmāṣapāda. He is known by the name Mitrasaha also.

## \|\| 2.63.177 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhastu mahātejāḥ kṣetre kalmāṣapādake \|*  
*aśmakaṃ janayāmāsa tvikṣvākukulavṛddhaye \|\| 177 \|\|*

177\. For the perpetuation of the line of Ikṣvāku, Vasiṣṭha of great brilliance, begot Aśmaka of the wife of Kalmāṣapāda.

## \|\| 2.63.178-179 \|\|

*aśmakasyauraso yastu mūlakastatsuto 'bhavat \|*  
*atrāpyudāharantīmaṃ mūlakaṃ vai nṛpaṃ prati \|\| 178 \|\|*

*sa hi rāmabhayādrājā strībhiḥ parivṛto 'vasat \|*  
*vivastrastrāṇamicchanvai nārīkavaca īśvaraḥ \|\| 179 \|\|*

178-179. Mūlaka was the bosom-born son of Aśmaka. In this context too they cite this, concerning king Mūlaka:—

“Indeed, because he was afraid of Paraśurāma, that king remained surrounded by women. Desirous of protection, the lord who was devoid of robes had women for his coat of mail.

## \|\| 2.63.180 \|\|

*mūlakasyāpi dharmātmā rājā śatarathaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasmācchatarathājjajñe rājā tviḍaviḍo balī \|\| 180 \|\|*

180\. The righteous-souled king Śataratha is remembered as the son of Mūlaka. Iḍaviḍa, the powerful king, was born of Śataratha.

## \|\| 2.63.181 \|\|

*āsīttvaiḍaviḍaḥ śrīmānkṛśaśarmā pratāpavān \|*  
*putro viśvasahasrasya putrīkasyāṃ vyajāyata \|\| 181 \|\|*

181\. The valorous Kṛtavarmā was the glorious son of Iḍaviḍa. His son Viśvasaha was born of Putrīkasī (?).

## \|\| 2.63.182-183 \|\|

*dilīpastasya putro 'bhūtkhaṭvāṅga iti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*yena svargādihāgatya muhūrttaṃ prāpya jīvitam \|\| 182 \|\|*

*trayo 'bhisaṃhitā lokā buddhyā satyena caiva hi \|*  
*dīrghabāhuḥ sutastasya raghustasmādajāyata \|\| 183 \|\|*

182-183. Dilīpa was his son. He became well known as Khaṭvāṅga. Having attained a span of life extending to a Muhūrta, he returned from Heaven and combined the three worlds on account of his intelligence and truthfulness. Dīrghabāhu was his son. Raghu was born of him.

## \|\| 2.63.184 \|\|

*ajaḥ putro raghoścāpi tasmājjajñe sa vīryavān \|*  
*rājā daśaratho nāma ikṣvākukulanandanaḥ \|\| 184 \|\|*

184\. Aja was the son of Raghu. The heroic king named Daśaratha was born of him. He was the delighter of the members of the family of Ikṣvāku.

## \|\| 2.63.185 \|\|

*rāmo dāśarathirvīro dharmajño lokaviśrutaḥ \|*  
*bharato lakṣmaṇaścaiva śatrughnaśca mahābalaḥ \|\| 185 \|\|*

185\. Rāma, Bharata, Śatrughna and Lakṣmaṇa of great strength were the sons of Daśaratha. Rāma was heroic, conversant with Dharma and well-known in the worlds.

## \|\| 2.63.186 \|\|

*mādhavaṃ lavaṇaṃ hatvā gatvā madhuvanaṃ ca tat \|*  
*śatrughrena purī tatra mathurā viniveśitā \|\| 186 \|\|*

186\. Śatrughna went to Madhuvana and killed Lavaṇa, son of Madhu. There the city of Mathurā was founded by Śatrughna.

## \|\| 2.63.187 \|\|

*subāhuḥ śūrase naśca śatrughnasya sutāvubhau \|*  
*pālayāmāsatustau tu vaidehyau mathurāṃ purīm \|\| 187 \|\|*

187\. Subāhu and Śūrasena were the sons of Śatrughna. They were born of the princess of Videha. They ruled over the city of Mathura.

## \|\| 2.63.188 \|\|

*aṅgadaścandraketuśca lakṣmaṇasyātmajāvubhau \|*  
*himavatparvatasyānte sphītau janapadau tayoḥ \|\| 188 \|\|*

188\. Aṅgada and Candraketu were the two sons of Lakṣmaṇa. Their territories at the border of the Himalaya mountain were very prosperous and flourishing.

## \|\| 2.63.189 \|\|

*aṅgadasyāṅgadākhyātā deśe kārayate purī \|*  
*candraketostu vikhyātā candracakrā purī śubhā \|\| 189 \|\|*

189\. In the territory of Kārāpatha (?) the city of Aṅgada was called Aṅgada. Candracakra, the splendid city of Candraketu is well known.

## \|\| 2.63.190 \|\|

*bharatasyātmajau vīrau takṣaḥ puṣkara eva ca \|*  
*gāndhāraviṣaye siddhe tayoḥ puryo mahātmanoḥ \|\| 190 \|\|*

190\. The heroic Takṣa and Puṣkara were the sons of Bharata. The cities of those two noble souls were situated in the realm of the Gandharvas.

## \|\| 2.63.191 \|\|

*takṣasya dikṣu vikhyātā nāmnā takṣaśilā purī \|*  
*puṣkarasyāpi vīrasya vikhyātā puṣkarāvatī \|\| 191 \|\|*

191\. The city of Takṣa was well known in all the quarters by the name of Takṣaśilā. The city of the heroic Puṣkara was well known as Puṣkarāvatī.

## \|\| 2.63.192 \|\|

*gāthāṃ caivātra gāyanti ye purāṇa vido janāḥ \|*  
*rāmeṇa baddhāṃ satyārthāṃ mahātmyāttasya dhīmataḥ \|\| 192 \|\|*

192\. Those people who are conversant with the Purāṇas sing this Gāthā (lyrical verse). It concerns Rāma. It consists of facts due to the greatness of that intelligent one.

## \|\| 2.63.193-195 \|\|

*śyāmo yuvā lohitākṣo dīptāsyo mītabhāṣitaḥ \|*  
*ājānubāhuḥ sumukhaḥ siṃhaskandho mahābhujaḥ \|\| 193 \|\|*

*daśavarṣasahasrāṇi rāmo rājyamakārayat \|*  
*ṛksāmayajuṣāṃ ghoṣo yo ghoṣaśca mahāsvanaḥ \|\| 194 \|\|*

*avyucchinno 'bhavadrājye dīyatāṃ bhujyatāmiti \|*  
*janasthāne vasankāryaṃ tridaśānāṃ cakāra saḥ \|\| 195 \|\|*
